2607.25886.description: RSIBench-Data evaluates LLM agents as data-centric researchers, where agents iteratively revise training-data strategies for a fixed target model on six benchmarks, with real training and evaluation runs.
2607.25886.whyItMatters: It isolates research capability from engineering, showing that current agents can improve from feedback but inconsistently. This provides an auditable testbed for capabilities needed in recursive self-improvement.
2607.25886.decisionReason: The paper provides a public GitHub repository with code and specifications for fixed post-training stack evaluation, enabling reuse.

2608.18607.description: VA-Judger-Bench evaluates reward models for joint video-audio generation. It contains paired comparisons of generated video-audio samples with human preference labels, covering in-domain and out-of-domain model outputs.
2608.18607.whyItMatters: Existing metrics evaluate quality dimensions separately, missing semantic and temporal coherence. VA-Judger-Bench provides a benchmark to assess whether reward models align with human preferences for joint video-audio generation.
2608.18607.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named evaluation object with a reproducible protocol, public data, and code for running or inspecting it.

2608.18701.description: SoftVTBench is a visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark for deformable-object manipulation, providing expert demonstrations with synchronized sensor data and finite-element ground truth, with a closed-loop evaluation protocol.
2608.18701.whyItMatters: Most manipulation benchmarks evaluate task success alone, ignoring physical interaction quality. SoftVTBench enables evaluation of deformation-aware success, addressing how policies interact with deformable objects.
2608.18701.decisionReason: No official code or data link is provided, so the public reuse path is not verified.

2608.18586.description: Diagnostic benchmark for handwritten OCR with six subtasks and 77.57K labeled images, evaluating MLLMs with five metrics.
2608.18586.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in OCR benchmarks by covering realistic handwriting scenarios, but without public artifacts, the reuse path is unclear.
2608.18586.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided in the paper; unclear if the benchmark is publicly accessible for other teams.

2608.18595.description: OdinEval is a benchmark for program repair in the Odin programming language, built from documented defects, with issue-to-commit bindings, regression tests, and execution records.
2608.18595.whyItMatters: Existing repair benchmarks focus on mainstream languages, leaving systems languages like Odin untested. OdinEval provides a reproducible benchmark for a less-covered language.
2608.18595.decisionReason: No official code or data link is provided, so the public reuse path is not verified.

2608.18704.description: Benchmark for multi-source memory fusion with synthesized scenarios and evidence-grounded questions.
2608.18704.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in evaluating memory systems for fragmented observations, but artifacts are not clearly available.
2608.18704.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided; unclear if benchmark is publicly accessible.

2608.18937.description: Benchmark for medical multimodal understanding and generation with 12 tasks and over 6M instances.
2608.18937.whyItMatters: Provides a broad benchmark for medical UAG, but without public access details, reuse is unclear.
2608.18937.decisionReason: No code or dataset links; benchmark accessibility is not specified.

2608.18618.description: Hierarchical benchmark for dexterous manipulation in laboratories, with real-world and simulation platforms.
2608.18618.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in evaluation for lab automation, but artifacts are not clearly available for reuse.
2608.18618.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided; unclear if benchmark is publicly accessible.

2608.18532.description: Diagnostic benchmark for hidden-state reasoning in long videos, with 1,427 video-QA instances.
2608.18532.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in evaluating spatiotemporal reasoning when objects are invisible, but public access is unclear.
2608.18532.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided; unclear if benchmark is accessible.

2608.18752.description: GreekBarRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark for Greek statutory articles, comprising bar-exam questions with case facts and candidate articles.
2608.18752.whyItMatters: Statutory retrieval for Greek is underexplored, and this benchmark provides a testbed for retrieval methods in a low-resource legal domain.
2608.18752.decisionReason: No official code or data link is provided, so the public reuse path is not verified.

2608.18993.description: ForeSightGuide is an anticipatory framework for visually impaired assistance, using vision-language models to predict hazards and filter alerts. It introduces a dataset for benchmarking predictive capabilities, but the paper focuses on the framework rather than a standalone benchmark.
2608.18993.whyItMatters: The framework addresses the problem of cognitive overload in assistive systems by providing anticipatory guidance. The introduced dataset could support development, but the primary contribution is the framework itself.
2608.18993.decisionReason: The dataset is introduced as part of a framework validation, not as a standalone public benchmark with a clear scoring contract or reuse path. No official code or data link is provided.

2608.18423.description: FM-Bench evaluates LLM agents on long-horizon football club management through 20 in-game years with 26 tools, measuring managerial decision quality via a deterministic engine scoring.
2608.18423.whyItMatters: Current agent benchmarks focus on bounded tasks, leaving long-horizon decision-making unmeasured. FM-Bench provides a reproducible environment with deterministic scoring to test sustained decision quality over hundreds of steps.
2608.18423.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named evaluation object with a deterministic engine, public code, and clear protocol for running and replaying evaluations.

2608.18534.description: FinRCA-Bench is a synthetic benchmark for financial reconciliation root-cause analysis, with 2,250 cases across 14 tables and 15 failure categories, providing evidence retrieval and reasoning evaluation.
2608.18534.whyItMatters: Financial AI systems need reliable evidence retrieval and reasoning, and existing benchmarks conflate the two. FinRCA-Bench separates retrieval evaluation from answer correctness.
2608.18534.decisionReason: The benchmark has a named dataset, deterministic generation, and public code for generating and evaluating.

2608.18554.description: CentaurBench evaluates LLM capabilities in both automating tasks and augmenting another agent's performance across seven real-world tasks, using blind pairwise comparisons by an LLM judge panel.
2608.18554.whyItMatters: It highlights that automation ability does not predict assistance quality, offering a framework for evaluating models in roles they play in human-AI systems. The approach could inform better model selection.
2608.18554.decisionReason: The paper describes a framework and experiments, but lacks clear public artifacts or instructions for reuse at this stage. No code or data link is provided, making it difficult to verify reproducibility.

2608.18591.description: BudgetDoc is a multimodal benchmark for estimating LLM reasoning performance under different budgets, supporting a DRB estimator for dynamic allocation. It includes three document tasks.
2608.18591.whyItMatters: It addresses the cost and over-thinking issues in inference by predicting performance across budget levels, enabling compute-optimal allocation. The approach could improve efficiency in document tasks.
2608.18591.decisionReason: While named a benchmark, the primary contribution is the DRB framework and dataset; the paper does not provide a clear public reuse path or ongoing scoring, and no artifacts are linked.

2608.18710.description: CamWorldQA is a benchmark for perceptual quality assessment of camera-controlled video generation, with 720 videos and human-rated scores. It supports a proposed CWQA network.
2608.18710.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in VQA for camera-controlled generation, focusing on viewpoint consistency and motion coherence. The dataset could aid development of specialized assessment methods.
2608.18710.decisionReason: The dataset is introduced to validate the CWQA method, lacking a standalone public comparison path. No data or code links are provided, and the benchmark is primarily a probe for the proposed approach.

2608.18451.description: The paper proposes DCGCNet, a deep learning model for atrial fibrillation detection from ECG signals, achieving state-of-the-art results across cross-dataset and noisy conditions.
2608.18451.whyItMatters: It introduces a robust method for AF detection, addressing variable leads and noise, with potential clinical deployment. However, it is not a benchmark but a model contribution.
2608.18451.decisionReason: The abstract describes a method and evaluation, not a benchmark with a reusable protocol. No public artifacts are provided for comparison.

2608.18726.description: AtmosCoder-Bench is an execution-grounded benchmark for LLMs on atmospheric science computation, with 436 problems and 3,910 variants, grading by executing code solutions against ground truth.
2608.18726.whyItMatters: Existing evaluations score final answers, overlooking calculation process. AtmosCoder-Bench makes process visible, revealing failures in applying formulas and adapting to regimes.
2608.18726.decisionReason: The benchmark has a defined protocol, public code, and public data for running evaluations.

2608.18588.description: AppEval is a benchmark for mobile application repair across HarmonyOS/ArkTS, iOS/Swift, and Android/Kotlin, using native toolchains and a common schema for build, install, launch, and test.
2608.18588.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap between repository-level repair evaluation and mobile build-install-launch-test boundaries, where infrastructure failures can be mistaken for program failures, but current quantitative findings are Android-specific.
2608.18588.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark, but without audited iOS and HarmonyOS results, the scoring contract is not fully specified across platforms, and no public artifacts are provided yet, making it unclear for public reuse.

2608.18675.description: An empirical benchmark comparing nine deep learning models for smart meter energy forecasting on two public datasets, analyzing input length, prediction horizon, architecture, and computational cost.
2608.18675.whyItMatters: It provides insights into model performance and trade-offs for energy forecasting, but does not define a repeatable evaluation object with a comparable scoring contract beyond standard metrics.
2608.18675.decisionReason: This is an empirical study comparing models, not a named benchmark with a defined protocol and public comparison path for other teams to run.

2608.17800.description: StartupBench is a benchmark for general-purpose agents on end-to-end workflows derived from market-validated AI startup products, with deliverable-oriented tasks and fine-grained rubrics.
2608.17800.whyItMatters: Existing agent benchmarks are researcher-selected, leaving real-world task performance uncertain. StartupBench measures agents on tasks with demonstrated demand.
2608.17800.decisionReason: No official data or code link is provided, so the public reuse path is not verified.

2608.17379.description: PTXBench evaluates LLMs in generating architecture-specific PTX for GPU kernel optimization. It measures functional correctness, execution of target instructions, and speedup over frontier libraries across GEMM and attention workloads on H100 and B200 GPUs.
2608.17379.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for LLM-driven GPU kernel optimization with architecture-specific PTX, providing a reproducible testbed to compare model capabilities and guide improvements in exploiting evolving GPU architectures.
2608.17379.decisionReason: PTXBench is an open-source environment with a reusable agent, benchmark implementation, and public data. It provides a clear evaluation protocol and scoring, making it a credible public benchmark for model comparison.

2608.17962.description: PRISM is a dataset of over 5,000 trajectories across 25 industrial manipulation tasks with multimodal sensing. It provides teleoperated demonstrations for contact-rich operations but lacks a standardized evaluation protocol or scoring contract.
2608.17962.whyItMatters: As a dataset, it could support research in contact-rich manipulation, but without a scoring mechanism it does not constitute a benchmark for model comparison.
2608.17962.decisionReason: The paper presents a dataset, not a benchmark with defined evaluation tasks and scoring. No scoring contract or comparison protocol is provided.

2608.17607.description: PathoArgus-Bench evaluates evidence-grounded visual reasoning in whole-slide pathology. It comprises 22,078 multiple-choice questions from 4,913 patients across 15 TCGA projects, testing availability, accessibility, use, and responsiveness of evidence under a fixed reader budget.
2608.17607.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap where final answer accuracy is insufficient to establish evidence grounding in pathology AI. Provides a protocol to assess whether models truly use supplied tissue evidence, offering a more rigorous evaluation for clinical deployment.
2608.17607.decisionReason: Provides a fixed benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol designed for evidence-grounded reasoning, with public data and clear methodology for reuse.

2608.17659.description: MobileWorldSafety evaluates GUI agents' safety against environmental injection attacks in Android apps. It includes 142 risk tasks on real applications, with programmatically verifiable risk indicators and a two-stage pipeline for verification.
2608.17659.whyItMatters: Provides a quantitative measure of GUI agent vulnerability to injection attacks, enabling comparison across agents and supporting development of safer mobile agents.
2608.17659.decisionReason: Provides a benchmark with defined tasks, scoring pipeline, and public code/data, allowing others to run and compare agents.

2608.17299.description: LiveHouse-TS is a living benchmark for time series foundation models, evaluating models prequentially on real future data across 11 domains and 17 datasets. It shifts benchmarking from snapshot accuracy to continuous temporal validity.
2608.17299.whyItMatters: Addresses the limitation of static benchmarks for time series models, providing a framework to assess model robustness under distribution shifts and long-term ranking stability.
2608.17299.decisionReason: Provides a live benchmark infrastructure with a public leaderboard and submission protocol, enabling ongoing model comparison.

2608.17600.description: LIBERO-VIFO is a benchmark for visual cue following in vision-language-action models, evaluating capability and safety across eight cue families. However, no public artifacts or official links are provided.
2608.17600.whyItMatters: If released, it could inform the development of safer VLA systems, but current lack of access limits its practical value.
2608.17600.decisionReason: No public benchmark artifacts or evaluation code are supplied, making it unclear how others can run or inspect the benchmark.

2608.17597.description: HarnessRisk evaluates agent harness safety across six lifecycle phases with 128 sandboxed cases. It measures Utility, Attack Success Rate, Persistence, and Detection for each trajectory.
2608.17597.whyItMatters: Addresses the need for systematic evaluation of agent harness safety across multiple responsibilities, enabling comparison of harness and model combinations and highlighting vulnerability patterns.
2608.17597.decisionReason: Provides a benchmark with defined cases, metrics, and public code/data enabling reproduction and comparison.

2608.17550.description: CADP-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs on compilable academic document parsing. It includes expert-verified full academic pages with tightly coupled text and structured elements, assessed through a re-injection compilation protocol.
2608.17550.whyItMatters: Provides a structured evaluation for structure-aware scientific document parsing, measuring the fidelity of executable reconstructions, which is crucial for machine-readable scientific knowledge.
2608.17550.decisionReason: Provides a benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol with public code and data, allowing reuse for measuring model capabilities in document parsing.

2608.17895.description: BEAR-Bench evaluates multimodal models on bilingual English-Russian text-dense business and scientific documents with 1,000 human-annotated questions.
2608.17895.whyItMatters: Existing multimodal benchmarks underrepresent bilingual professional document reasoning; BEAR-Bench targets this gap for enterprise and academic use cases.
2608.17895.decisionReason: No public benchmark artifacts or official dataset/code links are provided; scoring contract and reuse path are unclear.

2608.17271.description: ASI-Bench evaluates AI systems on 60 project-level scientific research tasks across 11 domains, with four guidance levels B1-B4 measuring autonomous execution and innovation.
2608.17271.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in evaluating AI's independent scientific exploration and execution, revealing current dependence on human guidance for end-to-end research.
2608.17271.decisionReason: Public project, code, datasets, and leaderboard are provided; scoring defined in B1-B4 conditions with fixed seeds and references.

2608.16081.description: SafeGesture evaluates vision-language models on scenario-conditioned safety interpretation of hand gestures, pairing 6 gestures with 8 scenarios for 4,800 items.
2608.16081.whyItMatters: It exposes a perception-reasoning gap in safety-critical gesture interpretation, providing a reusable test for scenario-dependent decision-making.
2608.16081.decisionReason: Public repository with fixed annotations, selected images, and scoring scripts; images require external HaGRID but identifiers are provided.

2608.16011.description: ReRef-3D benchmarks language-guided 3D scene rearrangement with 33,826 instructions across 998 scenes, evaluating placement validity and relation satisfaction.
2608.16011.whyItMatters: It targets spatial reasoning in embodied AI and provides metrics for relation satisfaction and physical validity in rearrangement tasks.
2608.16011.decisionReason: No public code or dataset links; evaluation pipeline not fully described; unclear how to reuse or reproduce.

2608.16645.description: Reconstruction is a blind benchmark for recovering research ideas from pre-publication bibliographies, using a judge model to match hypotheses.
2608.16645.whyItMatters: It tests idea recovery and anti-leakage protocols, but focuses on a specific research question rather than a general comparison.
2608.16645.decisionReason: Primarily supports the paper's finding on idea recovery; lacks a standalone public evaluation path and scoring contract.

2608.16717.description: PersonaShot benchmarks person-centric narrative continuity in multi-shot video generation with ~1,000 segments and 16 metrics.
2608.16717.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in evaluating character coherence across video cuts, including physical and emotional state continuity.
2608.16717.decisionReason: No public artifacts or code links; evaluator details and reuse path are not specified.

2608.17110.description: OV3D-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark for open-vocabulary monocular 3D detection, evaluating localization, semantic robustness, and cross-domain transfer across seven datasets.
2608.17110.whyItMatters: It reveals that open-vocabulary semantics is the primary bottleneck, providing a decoupled evaluation axis for detector diagnosis.
2608.17110.decisionReason: Public code repository exists; protocol replaces per-image oracles with dataset-level prompts and decouples metrics.

2608.16022.description: OpenHarmony Bench evaluates coding agents on 153 app-level ArkTS tasks across three input sources, with 242 feature points and device-based verification.
2608.16022.whyItMatters: It measures end-to-end app-level correctness, filling the gap between function-level coding benchmarks and real-world app development.
2608.16022.decisionReason: Official website, code, data, and leaderboard are provided; scoring via build and test pipeline with device execution.

2608.16203.description: INSPIRE evaluates instruction-aware speech retrieval, where natural-language instructions specify relevance criteria including semantic content, speaker identity, speaking style, environmental sounds, and combinations. The benchmark includes a fixed dataset and protocol for evaluating retrieval systems.
2608.16203.whyItMatters: Speech retrieval systems currently rely on fixed similarity matching and cannot adapt to diverse user intents. INSPIRE provides a standardized evaluation to compare methods across different retrieval intents, highlighting gaps in handling both semantic and paralinguistic attributes.
2608.16203.decisionReason: The paper introduces a benchmark with a clear evaluation object (instruction-aware speech retrieval), a defined scoring contract (retrieval paradigms evaluated), and a public dataset described as available. Although no explicit public reuse path is provided, the benchmark is intended for community use.

2608.16812.canonicalNameEvidence: we present ConceptEdit-Bench, a granular evaluation suite
2608.16812.description: A granular evaluation suite for image editing across over 1,000 fine-grained edit concepts, designed to diagnose model capabilities across real-world scenarios.
2608.16812.whyItMatters: Image editing lacks benchmarks that test fine-grained concept editing; this suite provides a way to assess model capabilities across a wide range of scenarios.
2608.16812.decisionReason: ConceptEdit-Bench is introduced in the paper without a standalone public comparison path. The GitHub repository primarily focuses on data generation, not a formal benchmark release with a stable scoring contract. The benchmark lacks a public evaluation protocol and standalone release, making it a viewpoint probe.

2608.16349.description: AeroCopilotBench is a two-tier benchmark for evaluating LLM agents as aviation copilots. Tier-1 uses 1,200 multiple-choice questions for knowledge assessment, while Tier-2 includes 73 procedural tasks in an interactive virtual cockpit environment, with safety-gated evaluation.
2608.16349.whyItMatters: Aviation evaluations often focus on static knowledge and cannot test procedural execution and safety compliance. AeroCopilotBench provides a reproducible interactive environment and safety-gated scoring to assess agents' task completion and trajectory safety.
2608.16349.decisionReason: The benchmark includes a reproducible environment (ACOE) and a public task set, with defined evaluation metrics. The environment and benchmark are intended for reuse by other teams.

2608.15654.description: WSE-bench evaluates LLM storytelling in open-ended world simulations, assessing three capacities: Generation Coverage (proportion of planned narrative steps), Consistency (canon coherence), and Richness (meaningful development). Uses a process benchmark to compare agent architectures.
2608.15654.whyItMatters: Storytelling evaluation has focused on finished stories, but open-ended narratives require sustained generation, coherence, and development. WSE-bench makes these dynamics visible and shows they are distinct capacities.
2608.15654.decisionReason: The benchmark is described as a process benchmark with specific metrics. It is intended for evaluation of LLM storytelling agents, but no public code or data is provided.

2608.15600.description: VARM-Bench evaluates verifiable structured reasoning in Chinese abusive-speech moderation. It uses field-anchored chain-of-thought rationales with six decision fields, and a deterministic protocol assessing field correctness, alignment, output validity, and record errors.
2608.15600.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks support classification but not verifiable reasoning. VARM-Bench provides an auditable protocol for evaluating moderation rationales, revealing that strong label performance can conceal errors in complete records.
2608.15600.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a unique evaluation object with deterministic scoring. It is described as reproducible and auditable, but no public link is provided.

2608.15555.description: RigidBench evaluates rigid-body physics in video generation models using a simulator-grounded benchmark with 100 examples and five tasks. It provides ten measurements covering motion, geometry, identity, background stability, and appearance, with per-frame data.
2608.15555.whyItMatters: Video generation metrics often mix independent errors. RigidBench separates these aspects and shows rankings depend on what is measured, providing a more detailed evaluation for physics fidelity.
2608.15555.decisionReason: The benchmark has a public GitHub repository, evaluation data on Zenodo, and clear instructions for reuse. It is a fixed dataset with a defined scoring contract.

2608.15931.description: PLSQLBench evaluates LLMs' ability to write executable PL/SQL programs through execution-based tests. It contains 2,865 instances including single-turn and multi-turn tasks, covering schema-grounded and procedural problems.
2608.15931.whyItMatters: Existing evaluations target general code generation or declarative text-to-SQL, leaving procedural database programming underexplored. PLSQLBench provides a benchmark for this capability, revealing gaps in schema grounding and dialect fidelity.
2608.15931.decisionReason: The benchmark is publicly available on GitHub with instructions for use. It has a stable scoring contract based on execution tests.

2608.15535.description: L3Cube-IndicQuest v2 is a multilingual QA benchmark for evaluating India-specific factual knowledge of LLMs. It contains 3,471 curriculum-grounded English QA pairs translated into 19 Indic languages, totaling 69,420 pairs across 20 languages.
2608.15535.whyItMatters: There is a need for benchmarks evaluating factual knowledge in Indic languages. This benchmark provides a large-scale gold-standard dataset with multiple evaluation protocols, showing consistent rankings across judges.
2608.15535.decisionReason: The benchmark is publicly released as a multilingual dataset. It is intended for evaluating LLMs' factual knowledge, with clear evaluation protocols.

2608.15539.description: CrossView is a multi-camera video question-answering benchmark spanning autonomous driving, security surveillance, egocentric/exocentric video, and robotics. It evaluates vision-language models on tasks that require joint reasoning across multiple simultaneous camera views, including resolving occlusions and integrating evidence across perspectives.
2608.15539.whyItMatters: Existing video benchmarks focus on single-camera settings, leaving multi-camera reasoning unmeasured. CrossView provides a standardized evaluation for a capability critical to real-world applications like autonomous vehicles and surveillance, enabling comparison of models on tasks that scale with viewpoint number and require cross-view integration.
2608.15539.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a clear evaluation object (multi-camera video QA), a defined scoring protocol (accuracy on held-out tasks), and a public path via the open-sourced code and dataset at the provided project page.

2608.15092.description: WeSCE is a benchmark for quantifying security drift in LLM-driven code editing. It consists of 400 executable programs derived from real-world code, covering feature addition, removal, bug fixing, and refactoring. The benchmark proposes a continuous risk representation and drift measures that capture changes in overall risk, worst-case severity, and vulnerability distribution.
2608.15092.whyItMatters: Code editing with weak-security constraints can introduce vulnerabilities, but existing evaluations lack a systematic measure. WeSCE offers a standardized way to quantify security drift, potentially aiding in selecting models and prompts that minimize security risks during code modifications.
2608.15092.decisionReason: The paper describes the benchmark and its components but does not provide an official link to the dataset, code, or evaluation protocol. The artifact evidence is empty, so public reuse and a stable scoring contract cannot be verified at this stage.

2608.15242.description: LongRCA Bench is a benchmark for diagnosing responsible roles and root causes in long-horizon agent failures. It comprises 1,140 failed trajectories across five domains, with human labels for the responsible role and the earliest decisive root-cause step. Evaluation focuses on responsible-role accuracy and exact root-step accuracy.
2608.15242.whyItMatters: Long-horizon agent failures are difficult to debug, and outcome-level metrics obscure where errors occur. LongRCA Bench provides a standardized testbed for failure attribution, enabling comparison of methods that localize root causes and assign responsibility, which is crucial for improving agent reliability.
2608.15242.decisionReason: The benchmark is explicitly named, has a clear evaluation object (failure diagnosis in agent trajectories), and provides a defined scoring protocol. The paper indicates the benchmark is publicly available, and the provided paper link serves as the official source.

2608.15064.description: LongDocBench is a benchmark for Table-of-Contents Hierarchy Recovery and Contextual Relationship Recovery in long documents. It includes 85 real-world documents (financial reports, textbooks, academic papers) spanning 2,582 pages, with human-verified annotations for 3,937 heading nodes and 3,258 contextual relationships.
2608.15064.whyItMatters: Existing document parsing benchmarks focus on page-level tasks, leaving document-level structure recovery unevaluated. LongDocBench provides a standardized evaluation for tasks that are critical for understanding long documents, enabling comparison of parsers on hierarchy and relationship recovery.
2608.15064.decisionReason: The benchmark is clearly defined with two tasks, provides a stable scoring protocol, and the paper states the dataset and evaluation protocol are publicly released, satisfying the public reuse path.

2608.15410.description: FloodReasonBench is a benchmark for vision-language model reasoning segmentation in flood response scenarios. It introduces FloodResponseSeg, a flood-specific dataset, and evaluates pipelines under lightweight visual encoding, split inference, and compressed representations. It also measures accuracy, latency, energy, and communication tradeoffs on an embedded platform.
2608.15410.whyItMatters: Reasoning segmentation for flood response has domain-specific constraints, and this benchmark characterizes model performance and system-level tradeoffs at the edge, which could inform deployment decisions for resource-constrained platforms.
2608.15410.decisionReason: The benchmark is presented as supporting the paper's findings on system-level tradeoffs; it lacks a clear standalone public comparison path as it is focused on a specific application and evaluation setup. The artifact evidence is empty, and no official dataset or code repository is provided.

2608.15177.description: FinFraudBench is a heterogeneous graph benchmark for financial fraud detection. It contains two datasets (CreditCard-Fraud and BankTrans-Fraud) with up to 8.99M nodes and 89.23M directed typed edges, preserving six financial entity types and fourteen edge types. The evaluation protocol covers ranking and imbalance-sensitive classification metrics.
2608.15177.whyItMatters: Existing graph-based fraud detection benchmarks often oversimplify financial systems and lack realistic conditions. FinFraudBench provides large-scale heterogeneous graphs with natural fraud rates, enabling more realistic evaluation of fraud detection methods and comparison across models.
2608.15177.decisionReason: The benchmark is named, has a clear evaluation object (fraud detection on heterogeneous graphs), and provides a standardized evaluation protocol. The dataset is available at the provided anonymous link, offering a public reuse path.

2608.15404.description: CBX-Bench is a benchmark for quantitatively measuring the quality of Concept Bottleneck Model (CBM) explanations. It uses a council of five open-weight multimodal LLMs to score explanations given an image and class, validated against human preferences. The benchmark maintains a leaderboard for CBM explanation quality.
2608.15404.whyItMatters: CBM interpretability is often evaluated by downstream accuracy, lacking quantitative measures of explanation quality. CBX-Bench offers a human-aligned, scalable evaluation that does not require concept ground truth, enabling comparison of explanation quality across different CBMs.
2608.15404.decisionReason: The benchmark is publicly hosted on GitHub with a leaderboard and submission path for new CBMs. The scoring protocol is defined and validated against human judgments, ensuring a stable scoring contract. The provided code repository and paper confirm the public reuse path.

2608.15127.description: AgentSysBench is a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit for characterizing agentic workloads on LLM serving systems. It includes ten representative agentic applications and unified instrumentation, identifying six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM inference.
2608.15127.whyItMatters: Serving systems are designed for conventional LLM inference and may not handle agentic workloads efficiently. AgentSysBench provides a measurement-based characterization that could guide system design for agentic applications.
2608.15127.decisionReason: The primary contribution is a characterization study of agentic workloads, not a standardized benchmark for model or system comparison. It does not provide a fixed dataset or protocol for scoring submissions, and no public reuse path is indicated.

2608.14270.description: TimeSage-EV evaluates LLM agents on time series analysis tasks in evolving environments, using 60 institutional scenarios across 6 domains with 1,485 scenario-period QA pairs. Agents receive data and reports, with withheld target releases as ground truth, assessing state identification, data summarization, and outlook reasoning.
2608.14270.whyItMatters: Existing time series QA benchmarks rely on fixed snapshots, but real-world data is released periodically, affecting conclusions. TimeSage-EV fills this gap by evaluating agentic temporal validity and cutoff-aware evidence use, providing a decision-value for deploying LLM agents in high-stakes domains where data updates matter.
2608.14270.decisionReason: Defines a live benchmark with a clear evaluation protocol, scoring on QA pairs, and provides monthly updates, code, and leaderboard, offering a credible public path for other teams to run or inspect.

2608.13990.description: SCOPE-Bench evaluates short-video recommendation systems by quantifying content depth using the Content Depth Score (CDS), a seven-level scale based on cognitive psychology. It provides CDS annotations for 150K videos from an open-source dataset, enabling systematic assessment of recommenders from a cognitive-content perspective.
2608.13990.whyItMatters: Existing short-video recommenders optimize for engagement, often favoring shallow content. SCOPE-Bench addresses the lack of benchmarks for content depth in recommendation, allowing evaluation of algorithms on their ability to recommend cognitively deep content, which has implications for user well-being and long-term engagement.
2608.13990.decisionReason: The paper defines a benchmark with a specific scoring metric (CDS), provides a large-scale annotated dataset, and includes a public project page with code and data, satisfying criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2608.14391.description: RA-Bench evaluates AI-generated video detection using real crisis-event videos as anchors. It includes 17,886 videos: 1,830 real anchors across 10 social-risk categories and 16,056 generated clips from nine generators. Detection is scored per source via AUC and TPR@5%FPR, with separate tracks for human-deceptive and dissemination-processed videos.
2608.14391.whyItMatters: Current detectors lack evidence on realistic AI-generated crisis videos. RA-Bench provides a matched real-generated evaluation to assess detector generalization, human perception, and robustness to social dissemination, supporting practical decisions on misinformation defense.
2608.14391.decisionReason: The benchmark has a clear evaluation object (video detection), a stable scoring protocol (source-matched, per-source metrics), and a public code repository with download and evaluation scripts, making it reusable by other teams.

2608.14329.description: Principle-Bench contains 168 cryptoasset financial-promotion scenarios mapped to two UK FCA principles, with paraphrase, adversarial keyword-stuffing, and boundary perturbations for evaluating LLM-as-judge on accuracy, paraphrase robustness, adversarial robustness, and calibration.
2608.14329.whyItMatters: Addresses the evaluation gap for LLM-as-judge in principle-based regulation, where standards are not binary. Provides a multi-axis assessment to inform deployment decisions, as no single method dominates all axes and adversarial inputs can significantly degrade performance.
2608.14329.decisionReason: Serves primarily as a viewpoint probe to support the paper's argument about evaluating LLM-as-judge; lacks a standalone public comparison path for other teams to run or inspect.

2608.14441.description: PACE-Bench is a simulator-grounded benchmark with 144 source-to-target adaptation pairs across six physics domains. Each pair presents a code-driven design that succeeds in a source environment but fails in a mutated target environment, and agents must iteratively adapt the design using diagnostic sandbox feedback within a limited attempt budget.
2608.14441.whyItMatters: Existing self-evolving agent evaluations assume fixed execution conditions and do not test recovery after environmental shifts. PACE-Bench provides a repeatable protocol to assess an agent's ability to adapt to changing physics, offering insight into the reliability of different self-evolving methods.
2608.14441.decisionReason: Public code repository with evaluation scripts, dataset, and documentation; fixed 144 pairs and attempt budget; scoring contract defined by success/failure in target environment.

2608.14015.description: MedClawBench evaluates long-horizon temporal reasoning in surgical videos through 1,123 doctor-grounded questions over self-built long neurosurgery recordings and a public lecture-video test split, with fixed evaluation dimensions for comparison.
2608.14015.whyItMatters: Existing VLM benchmarks fail to capture temporal dependencies in long surgical videos. MedClawBench provides a reproducible, doctor-grounded dataset to assess video reasoning capabilities beyond short clips, aiding progress in surgical AI systems.
2608.14015.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named evaluation object with a clear task (video question answering), a fixed dataset and protocol, and a credible public path via the project page and arXiv.

2608.14389.description: GBU-Palm is a large-scale multimodal video dataset for palm presentation attack detection, containing 21,326 videos from 105 subjects across six acquisition environments, including bona fide, Print, and Replay attacks, with 6,310 synchronized RGB-NIR samples. It evaluates video architectures under environment-matched and held-out-environment protocols, using metrics such as true accept, true reject, false accept, and false reject rates.
2608.14389.whyItMatters: Existing palm PAD datasets are limited by static imagery and restricted conditions, hindering systematic evaluation. GBU-Palm provides a unified benchmark to assess robustness across environments and modalities, helping practitioners choose architectures that generalize under environmental shift.
2608.14389.decisionReason: The paper introduces a named dataset and benchmark with clear evaluation protocols and public data, making it a reusable benchmark for other teams.

2608.14049.description: FlatLab is a simulation-based benchmark for robotic manipulation of flat objects, providing physical simulation, data collection, and standardized task definitions and evaluation protocols.
2608.14049.whyItMatters: It addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for flat object manipulation, a challenging domain due to ungraspable configurations and varied materials.
2608.14049.decisionReason: No public dataset or evaluation harness artifact verified; only a project page and paper, unclear access to benchmark code and data.

2608.14546.description: CPI-Bench evaluates image editing models across general, practical, and intelligent tasks with VLM-as-Judge scoring, including multi-image and reasoning-based editing.
2608.14546.whyItMatters: It provides a comprehensive benchmark that captures real-world deployment scenarios and reasoning demands, with scoring aligned to human preferences for reliable model comparison.
2608.14546.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository and Hugging Face dataset; clear evaluation protocol and scoring contract.

2608.14320.description: AnchorBench evaluates anchoring effects in LLMs across multiple pathways and anchor relevance, measuring answer shifts through controlled prompts.
2608.14320.whyItMatters: It addresses gaps in prior anchoring benchmarks by distinguishing irrelevant and plausible anchors and evaluating pathway dependence.
2608.14320.decisionReason: No public dataset or code artifacts; only paper text, unclear whether benchmark is accessible.

2608.13522.description: Vero evaluates repository-level verified code generation in Lean 4, with 43 multi-module instances, formal specifications, and proof-only and code-and-proof evaluation modes.
2608.13522.whyItMatters: It provides a testbed for measuring progress toward repository-scale verified software synthesis, where current agents fall short.
2608.13522.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository with benchmark instances, evaluation harness, and clear scoring contract.

2608.13221.description: TsuGO is a process-level reasoning benchmark for search efficiency in LLMs using Go life-and-death problems, parsing CoT into search trees and reporting diagnostics.
2608.13221.whyItMatters: It adds search organization as a missing evaluation dimension beyond final-answer accuracy in LLM reasoning benchmarks.
2608.13221.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links; unclear if benchmark is released.

2608.13167.description: TRAPSBench is a procedurally generated video benchmark with 1,404 physics pairs to test epistemic restraint in VLMs, using Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score (PECS).
2608.13167.whyItMatters: It highlights that VLMs can internally detect when abstention is required but fail to express it, offering a metric for calibration and restraint evaluation.
2608.13167.decisionReason: No public dataset or code artifacts; only paper report.

2608.13267.description: SciFigBench is a diagnostic VLM benchmark for scientific figure understanding, covering perception, reasoning, and behavioral reliability under uncertainty.
2608.13267.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in evaluating VLMs' behavior when visual evidence is missing or misleading, critical for scientific workflows.
2608.13267.decisionReason: No public dataset or evaluation harness accessible; only a project page.

2608.14741.description: PolyComp is a benchmark for compositional 3D spatial reasoning using polycube problems with 120 problems across four geometry families.
2608.14741.whyItMatters: It stresses visual recognition and compositional reasoning, with random guessing baseline at 25% for challenging multimodal evaluation.
2608.14741.decisionReason: No public artifacts; only paper text and no release link.

2608.13552.description: PlayWorld evaluates interactive video world models across 171 scenarios with long-horizon objectives. Agent players adaptively control each model, and performance is scored on geometry consistency, interaction fidelity, out-of-sight evolution, and insight evolution, plus basic video quality and controllability metrics.
2608.13552.whyItMatters: Standard fixed-action evaluations fail to compare world models that handle actions differently. PlayWorld provides an objective-driven protocol that reflects real user interaction, enabling fair cross-model assessment and highlighting limitations in spatial consistency and state evolution for long-horizon tasks.
2608.13552.decisionReason: The paper introduces a distinct benchmark with 171 scenarios, a defined agent-player protocol, and four core evaluation dimensions. Public code, dataset, and leaderboard provide a credible path for inspection and reuse.

2608.13210.description: NARU evaluates multimodal models on Japanese long-form video understanding across narrative evolution (character evolution, sequential flow, plot progression, thematic development) and cultural nuance (aizuchi, reading the air, subtext, cultural context, sentiment) via multiple-choice QA.
2608.13210.whyItMatters: NARU fills a gap in video QA benchmarks by jointly testing long-range narrative tracking and culturally grounded reasoning, which are absent in existing short-horizon or English-centric benchmarks. It provides a rigorous, reproducible protocol for measuring model capabilities in high-context media, supporting model development and product evaluation.
2608.13210.decisionReason: NARU has a defined task set (1,481 questions over 155 videos), a stable exact-match scoring contract, and a public code repository with lmms-eval integration and a Hugging Face dataset, enabling reproducible model comparison.

2608.13344.description: LongEarth-Bench evaluates vision-language models on long-horizon Earth observation reasoning, with ~120k QA samples from 117k images, sequences avg 15.14 frames (up to 30), covering 12 tasks in evolution summarization, spatial reasoning, anomaly identification, and logical prediction.
2608.13344.whyItMatters: LongEarth-Bench addresses the lack of benchmarks for long-sequence Earth observation reasoning, providing a more realistic and challenging evaluation for models designed to analyze multi-stage geographic changes.
2608.13344.decisionReason: The paper presents LongEarth-Bench, a large-scale benchmark with a clear evaluation protocol and publicly available data via arXiv/HuggingFace, making it reusable by other teams.

2608.13136.description: LigBench is an automated evaluation benchmark for AI research idea generation, using fine-grained and reliable evaluation across generation distributions. It includes PAIR-IQ, a dataset for training pairwise idea judgment models.
2608.13136.whyItMatters: Current evaluation of research idea generation is fragmented and lacks objective standards. LigBench aims to provide stable, interpretable, and expert-aligned assessments to support scalable and objective evaluation in this emerging area.
2608.13136.decisionReason: No official benchmark artifacts or public access paths are provided beyond the paper, and the named benchmark lacks a clear external comparison route, so the public comparison contract cannot be verified.

2608.12860.description: Evaluates vision-language navigation for humanoid robots across four embodiments in physics-grounded simulator scenarios. Includes 933 episodes with instructions and multiple stylistic variants, assessing success rate and normalized Dynamic Time Warping.
2608.12860.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in VLN benchmarks for bipedal locomotion and diverse morphologies, providing a platform to compare navigation models under physical constraints and supporting sim-to-real transfer studies.
2608.12860.decisionReason: Standalone benchmark with repeatable evaluation object and comparable scoring metrics, plus public release plan via official project page.

2608.12904.description: HounsBench is a CT-centric patient-state benchmark evaluating three task families: readout, reconstruction, and simulation. It provides patient-disjoint splits and per-family metrics for evaluating models on volumetric medical images and clinical language.
2608.12904.whyItMatters: HounsBench addresses the evaluation gap for CT-centered intelligence by unifying diverse tasks under a shared patient-state inference framework, enabling assessment of models that must integrate imaging and language for clinical decision support.
2608.12904.decisionReason: HounsBench is a named benchmark with a defined task protocol and split, and official code is provided, offering a public reuse path.

2608.13049.description: H2R-Bench evaluates cross-embodiment human-to-robot manipulation video generation. Models convert egocentric human demonstrations into robot manipulation videos under specified target embodiments. Scoring covers five dimensions: goal-state completion, action-event completion, functional contact transfer, embodiment correctness, and general video quality, aggregated into H2RCore.
2608.13049.whyItMatters: Assesses whether video world models can bridge the embodiment gap between human hands and robotic end-effectors, providing a diagnostic for how well generated videos transfer functional interactions and task execution. Results show generic video quality does not correlate with transfer validity, aiding model selection for robot learning from human video.
2608.13049.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined evaluation object (human-to-robot video generation), five scoring dimensions with weights, and a composite score. Public GitHub repository with project page, but evaluation code and annotations not yet included; quoted as 'not in this repository yet'. However, official project page and paper provide sufficient detail for replication, and repository is available for future updates. Public reuse path exists via project page and GitHub, though incomplete artifacts might warrant deferral. Given official links and clear protocol, decision is publish with public_reusable mode.

2608.13113.description: EgoMonth benchmarks month-level egocentric video understanding with 300+ hours from 20 participants over 20-120 days, 1,443 QA pairs, and a 14-task framework across schema consolidation, episodic indexing, and cascading reasoning.
2608.13113.whyItMatters: Existing long-video benchmarks lack inter-clip spatiotemporal continuity, so they cannot assess memory across days or weeks. EgoMonth provides a temporal-grounded evaluation for long-term memory in MLLMs, revealing that even top models remain far below human performance.
2608.13113.decisionReason: Defines a repeatable benchmark with a clear evaluation object, tasks, data, and human baseline, and provides public access via arXiv and Hugging Face.

2608.13441.description: Edit2TikZ evaluates instruction-guided scientific figure editing with TikZ code, featuring 1,548 samples with textual or visual localization requests and multi-step edits, using a human-aligned evaluation framework to measure edit completion and content preservation.
2608.13441.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on figure reconstruction or generation, leaving a gap for systematic evaluation of instruction-guided editing with compilable code. This benchmark provides a standardized protocol for assessing models' ability to perform precise, code-based edits while preserving unrelated content, offering practical value for developing reliable multimodal systems.
2608.13441.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset, evaluation protocol, and human-aligned scoring. Code and data are publicly available, providing a clear reuse path for other teams.

2608.12911.description: DocPrivacyBench evaluates susceptibility of document understanding MLLMs to relational privacy leakage when visual evidence is absent or minimal, using KIE tasks on identity documents.
2608.12911.whyItMatters: Addresses underexplored privacy vulnerabilities in document MLLMs, providing a framework to assess and mitigate leakage of correlated sensitive fields, which is crucial for trustworthy deployment in document processing.
2608.12911.decisionReason: No public access to the benchmark data or evaluation code is provided. The scoring contract and reuse path are unclear.

2608.12805.description: CoMedBench evaluates synthetic medical data fidelity and downstream utility across 37 dataset-task pairs from seven public sources, using a common clinical-validity framework and shared training and evaluation engine.
2608.12805.whyItMatters: Provides a reproducible benchmark for comparing synthetic data generators across multiple datasets and tasks, addressing the lack of comprehensive evaluation in prior studies and aiding in deciding when synthetic data is viable for model development.
2608.12805.decisionReason: No public access to the benchmark code, data, or evaluation tools is provided. The scoring contract is not specified in sufficient detail.

2608.12894.description: BavGround evaluates regional cultural grounding and dialect competence in Bavarian across English, German, and Bavarian, with 618 multi-parallel multiple-choice questions across eight cultural domains.
2608.12894.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in cultural evaluation for regional and dialect communities, providing a protocol-aware benchmark that highlights performance differences across evaluation methods and supports localized assessment of LLMs.
2608.12894.decisionReason: No public access to the benchmark data or evaluation protocols is provided. The scoring contract and reuse path are unclear.

2608.14718.description: VideoGAIA evaluates agentic video understanding through multi-turn, tool-augmented interactions where models must iteratively perceive videos, invoke external tools, and integrate multimodal evidence. It contains 271 human-verified tasks across diverse real-world scenarios.
2608.14718.whyItMatters: Conventional single-turn video understanding benchmarks are becoming saturated; VideoGAIA moves beyond to assess advanced MLLMs' ability to act as general AI assistants, using tools to gather complementary information across turns. It provides a timely, challenging benchmark for next-generation video understanding.
2608.14718.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset and evaluation framework. Code and dataset are publicly available, providing a clear path for other teams to run and inspect the benchmark.

2608.12549.description: StrAD is a benchmark for long-form audio description generation on full-length videos across diverse genres, reformulating the task as streaming dense video captioning without ground-truth timestamps.
2608.12549.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of evaluation for full-video AD generation, providing a measurable benchmark that includes both fine-tuned and zero-shot approaches, which is essential for scaling accessibility.
2608.12549.decisionReason: No public access to the benchmark data or evaluation scripts is provided. The scoring contract is not specified in enough detail.

2608.12654.description: SteerBench-Work evaluates agent steering decisions at action boundaries in workplace scenarios across seven domains, with 106 incident-anchored scenarios and evidence-reversed mirrors, scored on correct proceed/hold boundaries.
2608.12654.whyItMatters: Addresses the critical pre-commit decision in long-running agents, where a single step can have significant consequences. The benchmark reveals that models tend to over-refuse authorized actions, providing valuable insight for calibrating agent behavior to avoid both unsafe actions and unnecessary delays.
2608.12654.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset, clear scoring contract (proceed/hold accuracy), and public leaderboard at steerbench.com. Provides reusable path for other teams.

2608.11562.description: S2R-Bench evaluates video reflection removal, supporting full-reference and human perceptual assessment, and is used to validate the S2R-Removal model.
2608.11562.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of benchmarks for video reflection removal, providing a dedicated evaluation protocol that includes both synthetic and real-world scenarios, which is crucial for advancing this under-explored task.
2608.11562.decisionReason: No public access to the benchmark dataset or evaluation code is provided. The scoring contract is not detailed, and the reuse path is unclear.

2608.12004.description: RealisticTritonBench evaluates LLM-generated Triton kernels using tasks derived from real-world pull requests in popular AI frameworks, with end-to-end integration tests.
2608.12004.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on isolated kernel translation and may have flawed evaluation scripts, while this benchmark provides realistic tasks and robust end-to-end evaluation, offering more practical insight into LLM performance for production kernel development.
2608.12004.decisionReason: The paper defines a benchmark with a fixed task set and evaluation protocol, and the arXiv paper provides a public path for inspection and reuse.

2608.12197.description: NetlistBench evaluates LLM reliability in recognizing and manipulating SPICE netlists, covering parameter and connectivity recognition, edits, hierarchical operations, equivalence judgment, and compound editing, with deterministic structure-aware scoring.
2608.12197.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in assessing LLM reliability for simulator-facing netlist tasks, distinct from high-level design reasoning, and provides a structured evaluation to guide trustworthy circuit design automation.
2608.12197.decisionReason: No public artifacts or hosting links beyond the paper are provided, so the public reuse path is not verifiable.

2608.11584.description: The benchmark evaluates LLM instruction adherence and robustness in enterprise retrieval scenarios, using 983 expert-validated samples across six domains, simulating retrieval noise, knowledge gaps, and factual conflicts.
2608.11584.whyItMatters: Existing RAG benchmarks assume clean retrieval and simple queries, failing to capture production conditions. This benchmark addresses the gap by measuring holistic compliance under non-ideal conditions, informing deployment decisions for enterprise-scale RAG systems.
2608.11584.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links to the benchmark or evaluation framework are provided; the release is planned for the future, so the benchmark is not yet publicly usable or inspectable.

2608.12262.description: Diagram-MMU evaluates multimodal language models on parsing scientific diagrams into LaTeX TikZ code, editing diagram code, and answering questions about diagrams, using 3.7k diagrams and 18.3k questions across six domains.
2608.12262.whyItMatters: The evaluation provides insight into model capabilities on diagram-to-code generation tasks, a practical need in scientific authoring tools, and identifies gaps between reasoning and code generation.
2608.12262.decisionReason: The paper's primary contribution is the evaluation and findings about model performance under agentic settings, but the benchmark lacks a stated public reuse path for other teams to run or inspect it.

2608.12002.description: Evaluates AI agents on telecom network troubleshooting tasks, focusing on root cause analysis and path restoration, using expert-grounded metrics.
2608.12002.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in evaluating AI agents for realistic telecom operations, emphasizing evidence-based diagnosis and practical constraints.
2608.12002.decisionReason: Insufficient artifact evidence and no official benchmark repository or leaderboard link provided to confirm public availability.

2608.14721.description: AeroGround evaluates vision-language models on aerial-ground collaborative reasoning using a simulated dataset of ~29,000 multimodal observation groups and 2,250 QA instances covering cross-view correspondence, spatial understanding, and reasoning.
2608.14721.whyItMatters: Existing UAV benchmarks focus on aerial-only views; AeroGround fills the gap for aerial-ground collaboration, offering a standardized evaluation for models in real-world applications like rescue and inspection, with clear human performance comparison.
2608.14721.decisionReason: The paper introduces a new benchmark with a fixed dataset and protocol, providing a public path via the arXiv paper and associated resources, enabling other teams to evaluate models.

2608.10359.description: VoxSumm evaluates joint summarization and translation of long-form spoken news. It comprises 10,045 BBC article-summary pairs across 24 languages and about 703 hours of speech, with scoring based on summarization and translation quality.
2608.10359.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks treat long-document summarization and speech translation separately, leaving a gap for cross-lingual summarization of spoken content. VoxSumm provides a publicly inspectable resource for developing systems that compress and translate long-form speech, aiding evaluation of multilingual instruction-following and cross-lingual generation.
2608.10359.decisionReason: VoxSumm is a defined multilingual corpus with a scoring protocol for joint summarization and translation, and the corpus is released publicly for reuse, meeting the criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2608.10408.description: VisEditBench is a benchmark comprising 1,395 human-annotated visualization code-editing tasks across two settings: feedback-guided repair and reference-guided restyling. Models are evaluated on their ability to revise existing visualization code based on multimodal feedback such as buggy or marked charts with textual instructions, and target chart images. Scoring is based on pass rates of generated code executions.
2608.10408.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on generating visualizations from scratch, leaving the iterative editing process unexplored. VisEditBench provides a standardized evaluation for this practical task, enabling comparisons across VLMs and highlighting gaps in open-source models, particularly in visually grounded style adaptation.
2608.10408.decisionReason: The paper defines a clear evaluation object with 1,395 tasks, a comparable scoring contract (pass rates), and a publishable GitHub repository with the benchmark, satisfying the criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2608.10875.description: VibeLifeBench evaluates LLM agents on 200 long-horizon, multi-week tasks across 10 everyday-life domains in a simulated world of 22 mock services. Agents must manage silent world changes and implicit constraints, with fine-grained weighted checks on end state, timeliness, and constraint adherence.
2608.10875.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on short, static tasks, leaving a gap in measuring long-horizon proactive assistance. VibeLifeBench provides a credible public evaluation for agents that must operate over weeks with changing environments, offering practical decision value for deploying personal assistants.
2608.10875.decisionReason: Official code repository with runnable open subset and scoring contract; tasks are scripted timelines with atomic checks, suitable for ongoing comparison.

2608.10414.description: Evaluates LLM robustness to Vietnamese dialectal rewrites across emotion recognition, natural language inference, question answering, and multiple-choice QA, measuring performance degradation across six dialect groups.
2608.10414.whyItMatters: Highlights that model performance on standard Vietnamese does not guarantee reliable behavior under regional variation, informing deployment decisions for Vietnamese-language applications.
2608.10414.decisionReason: No official benchmark link or public dataset repository provided; the benchmark appears primarily to support the paper's evaluation findings without a standalone public comparison path.

2608.11452.description: TangPoetryBench evaluates text-to-image models on illustrating classical Chinese Tang poems across ten human-annotated dimensions, with a rubric-conditioned evaluator (PAE).
2608.11452.whyItMatters: Existing metrics fail to capture cultural and emotional fidelity in poetry-to-image generation; this benchmark provides a multi-dimensional human-annotated dataset and an automated evaluator to support model comparison in this niche domain.
2608.11452.decisionReason: No official benchmark URL or public access point is provided; artifact evidence is empty, so the public reuse path is unclear.

2608.11469.description: SRE-Bench evaluates AI agents on reverse engineering of binaries compiled from 19 private real-world-scale C programs (average 16.9K LoC) with 44 anti-analysis primitives, yielding 262 binary instances and 1572 deterministically graded tasks.
2608.11469.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks for agentic cybersecurity miss either contamination control or realistic scale. SRE-Bench addresses this gap by combining private, real-world-scale binaries with deterministic grading, enabling reliable measurement of agent performance in binary analysis and highlighting the gap between source-code and binary security capabilities.
2608.11469.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named benchmark (SRE-Bench) with a clear evaluation object (reverse engineering), a repeatable protocol (deterministic grading tasks), and a public path via the arXiv paper. It is not merely a probe for one paper's finding. Public reuse is feasible through the detailed description and artifacts indicated by the paper, despite no direct artifacts listed.

2608.10692.description: SPIEval is a human-curated benchmark for evaluating large language models as mobile assistants that retrieve and reason over personal information scattered across multiple apps. It comprises 250 tasks across five cognitive capabilities, 4,335 fictional personal records in 10 simulated apps, and supports multi-turn interaction through 21 tools. Models receive underspecified user instructions and must search records and invoke tools; final execution calls are compared to human-annotated gold calls at the parameter level.
2608.10692.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks do not target the challenge of leveraging scattered personal information across apps in mobile assistant settings. SPIEval provides a controlled, verifiable evaluation environment grounded in five cognitive capabilities, enabling assessment of model capabilities in realistic mobile contexts. The reported results show substantial room for improvement and highlight fundamental limitations in information localization and search efficiency, offering practical guidance for deploying LLM-based assistants.
2608.10692.decisionReason: The dataset and code are publicly available on Hugging Face, with a detailed README specifying tasks, tools, evaluation protocol, and leaderboard. The scoring contract is parameter-level comparison against gold calls, stable and repeatable. The benchmark is a standalone, reusable public resource, not solely supporting a paper's viewpoint.

2608.11149.description: PRMU evaluates corpus-free multimodal unlearning of person-related knowledge in MLLMs, using textual and visual probes including adversarial evaluation and locality analysis.
2608.11149.whyItMatters: Addresses realistic deletion scenarios where original corpora are unavailable, providing a way to measure forgetting-locality trade-offs and vulnerability to knowledge reactivation, which is valuable for safe deployment.
2608.11149.decisionReason: Code is not yet released and the paper reports future release, so public reuse path is not currently available; scoring details and protocol are not fully specified in the supplied text.

2608.10444.description: MPAR-Bench evaluates multi-point associative reasoning in LLMs across English and Chinese using 1,000 items with diverse clues. Scoring includes exact-match accuracy, ANLS, embedding similarity, and reasoning-trace verification, with four perturbation types.
2608.10444.whyItMatters: Current benchmarks focus on reasoning depth (longer chains) but neglect breadth (parallel semantic exploration). MPAR-Bench fills that gap, showing that depth does not guarantee robust breadth, and offers a practical tool for assessing models on a complementary reasoning dimension.
2608.10444.decisionReason: MPAR-Bench provides a fixed dataset of 1,000 items with scoring protocols and perturbation analyses, and the paper and official links offer a credible public path for reuse.

2608.11434.description: MobileJudgeBench evaluates LLM-as-judge methods on mobile agent trajectories. It includes 931 human-annotated trajectories from 6 mobile agent benchmarks, covering 4 agent models and 68 apps.
2608.11434.whyItMatters: Mobile agent benchmarks increasingly rely on LLM-based judges, yet their reliability is unexamined. MobileJudgeBench fills this gap by providing a standardized evaluation to select reliable judges, improving evaluation fidelity and downstream reinforcement learning.
2608.11434.decisionReason: The paper presents a named benchmark (MobileJudgeBench) with a clear evaluation object (LLM judges on trajectories), a scoring contract (accuracy against human annotations), and a public path via the arXiv paper and Hugging Face page. The artifact evidence is not required as the paper provides sufficient protocol details.

2608.10396.description: The paper introduces FormStruct-Bench, an evaluation dataset for table-form document structure recognition, but no official links to the benchmark artifacts are provided.
2608.10396.whyItMatters: An evaluation gap exists between holistic document outputs and fine-grained structural scores, but the lack of public benchmark access limits its practical utility.
2608.10396.decisionReason: No public benchmark artifact or official repository link is provided in the input; the paper text alone does not establish a standalone public comparison path.

2608.10916.description: A benchmark for evaluating faithfulness of mathematical chain-of-thought autoformalisation, using perturbed reasoning steps to test validity and invalidity preservation.
2608.10916.whyItMatters: Addresses the need for sound and cheap evaluation of autoformalisation faithfulness, revealing sycophancy in current systems.
2608.10916.decisionReason: The benchmark is primarily a probe to support the paper's findings, with no clear standalone public comparison path or evidence of public availability.

2608.10366.description: DSAgentBench evaluates language agents on end-to-end data-science workflows in real computer environments. It comprises 275 tasks spanning data wrangling, exploration, modeling, visualization, and validation, with deterministic evaluators verifying analytical correctness, visual outputs, and model performance.
2608.10366.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks lack real-computer interaction and fail to capture the multi-stage, multi-tool nature of data-science practice. DSAgentBench provides a realistic environment for assessing whether agents can automate complete workflows, highlighting a significant capability gap and offering a foundation for developing grounded, verifiable autonomous agents.
2608.10366.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a public repository, clear task set, and deterministic evaluators; provides a credible path for others to run or inspect it.

2608.11154.description: CriticalSCM-Bench v1 is a synthetic supply-chain benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. It evaluates intervention ranking policies across semiconductor, critical-material, and digital-infrastructure archetypes under partial and delayed information, with stress tests on fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions.
2608.11154.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the gap between detection and decision by quantifying recoverable net value of interventions, helping choose between adaptive ranking and simpler structural policies based on domain conditions and out-of-distribution robustness.
2608.11154.decisionReason: Provides a reproducible benchmark with official code repository, defined evaluation protocol, and stored outputs for verification; public reuse path is clear.

2608.10677.description: Chartography evaluates vision-language models on 100 chart-understanding tasks sourced from professional practice, with questions authored by domain experts and triple-verified. The benchmark uses pass@1 accuracy as the scoring metric across 30 frontier model configurations.
2608.10677.whyItMatters: Existing chart benchmarks are saturated and skewed toward simple formats, leaving a gap in measuring performance on realistic, domain-specific charts. Chartography provides a harder, expert-validated test that can differentiate model capabilities in high-stakes professional contexts.
2608.10677.decisionReason: The paper defines a fixed set of 100 tasks with a clear pass@1 scoring protocol and releases tasks, images, and evaluation code, providing a credible public reuse path for other teams.

2608.11074.description: CapProbe is a full-scene dense QA benchmark for evaluating detailed image captions from Vision-Language Models. It decomposes images into semantic regions and generates multiple-choice questions across 10 semantic categories, with a language judge answering from captions. The benchmark comprises 346 images, 1,868 regions, and 25,650 questions.
2608.11074.whyItMatters: Existing metrics for detailed caption evaluation struggle to verify dense factual claims. CapProbe addresses this by region-aligned factual checking with dense QA, offering a cost-effective protocol that reduces open-ended scoring bias and reveals coverage gaps and trade-offs across models.
2608.11074.decisionReason: The data, annotations, and evaluation code are not yet released; only 'will be released soon'. Public reuse path is not yet available, and the scoring contract may depend on the judge. Defer until artifacts are available.

2608.09573.description: Evaluates video-grounded diagnostic understanding of one-shot website generation. Approximately 1.7K Video QA instances from 6,338 verified failures across semantic-logical, visual-motion, structural-temporal, and functional categories. Scoring is based on model accuracy in multi-agent system V2Lens compared against baseline Video MLLMs.
2608.09573.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks often score isolated artifacts or final outcomes, lacking diagnostic insight. This benchmark provides a repeatable protocol to assess failure modes in generated webpages, enabling targeted model improvements for interactive website generation.
2608.09573.decisionReason: Defines a fixed dataset of 1.7K video QA instances with a clear scoring contract, publicly released via arXiv and Hugging Face paper page, and usable by other teams.

2608.10042.description: UserToolBench evaluates personalized decision making in tool-use LLMs through inference of latent user preferences, clarification need, and user-aligned tool-call trajectories, built from privacy-sanitized interaction traces with 10 user profiles, 36 tool sets, and 1,065 turns.
2608.10042.whyItMatters: Current personalization benchmarks focus on surface-level style imitation or response personalization, not whether models make correct decisions for the user. UserToolBench addresses this gap by emphasizing decision quality, which is critical for real-world delegation tasks.
2608.10042.decisionReason: Benchmark lacks public reusable artifacts and clear scoring contract; primarily supports the paper's findings without a standalone public comparison path.

2608.09538.description: Evaluates LLMs on research-level theoretical computer science proof generation, using theorem-proving tasks from papers at STOC, FOCS, and SODA. Provides context for self-contained proofs and uses a verification agent to check correctness.
2608.09538.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in evaluating LLMs on advanced formal reasoning in theoretical computer science, offering a structured protocol with a verification agent that aligns closely with expert judgment, supporting reliable model comparison.
2608.09538.decisionReason: The paper introduces a new benchmark with a clear task design, a verification-based scoring contract, and evidence of a reusable public path through ArXiv and Hugging Face.

2608.10258.description: TAF-MED is a physician-reviewed benchmark of 500 fixed three-turn medical safety scenarios, evaluating LLM responses for unsafe guidance across multi-turn dialogues.
2608.10258.whyItMatters: Addresses the evaluation gap where first-turn safety is an incomplete proxy for conversational safety persistence, providing a protocol for assessing model behavior across complete dialogue trajectories in medical contexts.
2608.10258.decisionReason: The benchmark is described with a fixed set of scenarios and rubric, indicating a stable scoring contract. However, the public reuse path is not yet available as the dataset is only planned for release on Hugging Face, with no current link. Evidence insufficient for public_reusable.

2608.09802.description: A multilingual code refactoring benchmark with 170 instances drawn from real commits across seven programming languages. Evaluates AI agents on large-scale refactoring tasks averaging 11.4 modified files and 261.6 lines of code, using manually curated issue descriptions and test suites.
2608.09802.whyItMatters: Existing software engineering benchmarks face saturation and quality issues, with flawed tests and training data leakage. This benchmark provides a more challenging and realistic refactoring task set with rigorous curation, offering a robust measure of agent capability for long-horizon coding tasks.
2608.09802.decisionReason: The dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face, provides evaluation scripts and Docker-based runner, and specifies a clear scoring contract (pass@1 via patch-based evaluation). It is designed for ongoing maintenance with a v2 planned, indicating a public comparison path.

2608.09873.description: Sci-VBench evaluates text-to-video generation across 1,253 expert-annotated examples in 60 scientific subjects. It requires temporally rich videos demonstrating scientific reasoning and knowledge-grounded synthesis. Scoring covers four dimensions: prompt grounding, scientific correctness, spatiotemporal consistency, and low-level perceptual fidelity, using a rubric-based protocol with MLLM judges.
2608.09873.whyItMatters: Existing video generation benchmarks focus on surface realism, leaving scientific and causal correctness unmeasured. Sci-VBench provides a public protocol and open dataset to compare models on knowledge-intensive generation, revealing gaps between visual quality and reliable scientific dynamics.
2608.09873.decisionReason: Named benchmark with explicit evaluation object (science video generation), defined scoring contract (rubric-based dimensions), and public code, dataset, and scorer enabling reproducible runs.

2608.09230.description: SafeSceneReason evaluates multimodal industrial-safety reasoning with 123,695 question-answer pairs covering compliance, hazard interaction, accident mechanisms, and prevention recommendations across scene-centric and report-centric pipelines.
