2605.26667.whyItMatters: Existing memory benchmarks report aggregate QA accuracy, failing to attribute errors to specific system components. MemFail provides fine-grained diagnostics for memory system design.
2605.26667.decisionReason: No public artifacts or code provided; unclear how to run or inspect the benchmark.

2605.28876.description: Benchmark evaluating 11 log reduction tools on 35 GitHub Actions failure cases, scored by 3 LLM debugger families.
2605.28876.whyItMatters: No public comparison existed for which log reductions preserve diagnostic evidence for LLM-based root-cause diagnosis.
2605.28876.decisionReason: Public data, code, per-case bundles, and reproducibility infrastructure are provided.

2605.26781.description: Dynamic benchmark for multimodal reasoning on high school exam questions in math, physics, chemistry, and biology, with a mock exam evaluation scheme.
2605.26781.whyItMatters: Static benchmarks are prone to contamination and fail to reflect real exam constraints. LiveK12Bench provides a growing, realistic evaluation for educational readiness.
2605.26781.decisionReason: Code and dataset are publicly available.

2605.27074.description: Benchmark for interactive proactive intelligence of MLLMs under streaming video, covering proactive monitoring, task management, and interleaved requests.
2605.27074.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks overlook dynamic multi-turn proactive interactions. IPIBench fills this gap for streaming assistant evaluation.
2605.27074.decisionReason: No public dataset or code provided; unclear how to run or inspect the benchmark.

2605.27240.description: Benchmark for emotional need-aware proactive memory retrieval in support agents, with 1,800+ dialogues mapped to Maslow's hierarchy.
2605.27240.whyItMatters: Current memory retrieval is factual, neglecting emotional needs. ENPMR-Bench evaluates proactive retrieval for empathetic interaction.
2605.27240.decisionReason: No public artifacts or code provided; unclear how to run or inspect the benchmark.

2605.26918.description: Benchmark for educational validity of video generation models, grounded in the Knowledge-Skills-Attitude framework.
2605.26918.whyItMatters: Existing video benchmarks ignore pedagogical validity, which is critical for classroom use. EduVideoBench fills this gap.
2605.26918.decisionReason: No public dataset or code provided; unclear how to run or inspect the benchmark.

2605.27759.description: Simulation benchmark for VLA generalization with 28 tasks across 13 categories and two robot morphologies, using ManiSkill.
2605.27759.whyItMatters: VLA models often fail under distribution shifts. Colosseum V2 provides standardized in/out-domain evaluation for reproducible comparison.
2605.27759.decisionReason: Built on ManiSkill simulator; code and data are publicly available.

2605.26994.description: Interactive benchmark for dynamic chart understanding requiring GUI actions to obtain evidence, with 673 charts and 1,440 QA pairs.
2605.26994.whyItMatters: Existing chart benchmarks are static; ChartAct evaluates models on real interactive environments, crucial for real-world chart use.
2605.26994.decisionReason: Public code repository with dataset and evaluation infrastructure.

2605.27472.description: Evaluates LLM generation of SystemVerilog assertions from structured design specifications and RTL, across two tasks: bug-prevention and bug-hunting. The benchmark includes 83 real-world designs with golden and mutated RTL, and assesses syntactic validity, formal provability, coverage, and mutation-based bug detection.
2605.27472.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in realistic evaluation for assertion generation by using full specifications and buggy RTL, supporting comparison of LLM capabilities for hardware verification tasks.
2605.27472.decisionReason: Public benchmark with fixed dataset and protocol; evaluation metrics are defined; open-source and reproducible.

2605.27761.description: AndroidDaily evaluates mobile GUI agents on 350 daily-use tasks across 94 closed-source Android applications. Automatic scoring is based on a three-tiered guideline system (operational obligations, output quality, negative constraints), with step-level diagnostic judgments.
2605.27761.whyItMatters: Fills evaluation gap for real-world closed-source apps where internal states are unavailable, providing a verifiable scoring method based on observable guidelines. Useful for assessing practical deployment of GUI agents.
2605.27761.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear task set, evaluation protocol, and automatic scoring contract. Public details in paper and on arXiv allow inspection.

2605.26068.description: WSADBench is a benchmark for weakly supervised anomaly detection (WSAD) that unifies evaluation across incomplete, inexact, and inaccurate supervision scenarios. It evaluates 36 algorithms across 4 modalities (tabular, video, image features, text embeddings) by systematically varying label quantity, granularity, and quality, with protocols and code provided.
2605.26068.whyItMatters: The field of weakly supervised anomaly detection has lacked a unified evaluation framework, with existing benchmarks isolating the three supervision types. WSADBench provides a standardized comparison that reveals performance boundaries across scenarios and informs algorithm selection for practitioners facing limited or noisy labels.
2605.26068.decisionReason: The benchmark is a comprehensive, publicly released evaluation object with a detailed GitHub repository, code, datasets, and standardized protocols. It enables other teams to run experiments and compare methods across multiple modalities and supervision settings.

2605.25874.description: WBench evaluates interactive video world models across five dimensions: video quality, setting adherence, interaction adherence, consistency, and physics compliance. It includes 289 test cases and 1,058 multi-turn interaction sequences, covering diverse scenes and control types, with 22 automatic sub-metrics validated against human judgment.
2605.25874.whyItMatters: No unified standard previously existed for evaluating interactive world models across the required competencies. WBench provides a comprehensive, multi-turn benchmark with a public leaderboard and open data/code, enabling systematic model comparison and diagnostic insights into strengths and weaknesses.
2605.25874.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation object with 289 test cases and 1,058 interaction turns, provides a comparable scoring contract with 22 validated metrics, and offers public code, data, and a leaderboard, qualifying as a score_submission benchmark.

2605.25388.description: ViroBench evaluates nucleotide foundation models on viral genomics tasks across two axes: biological understanding (taxonomy classification, host prediction) and latent biosecurity risk (genome modeling, CDS completion). It includes 18 tasks, 58,314 viral samples, multiple split strategies (genus-disjoint, temporal), and 11 metrics, with a unified evaluation protocol and leaderboard.
2605.25388.whyItMatters: Viral genomics lacks a unified evaluation standard for foundation models. ViroBench provides a diagnostic benchmark that measures both task performance and biosecurity risk, enabling model comparison and guiding development of safer, more robust viral nucleotide models.
2605.25388.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a clear evaluation object (viral sequence tasks), a comparable scoring contract (unified metrics and splits), and a public path for reuse via code and dataset links. It is an ongoing benchmark with a leaderboard.

2605.25784.description: VertiCue-Bench evaluates multimodal large language models on geospatial reasoning using canopy height models to resolve 2D ambiguity in remote sensing natural scenes. It includes 1,534 instances across 17 tasks, testing height perception and semantic reasoning.
2605.25784.whyItMatters: Current remote sensing benchmarks are mostly 2D-centric, failing in environments with spectral confusion. This benchmark addresses the gap of whether models can leverage vertical cues for semantic disambiguation, providing insights into geometry-to-semantics reasoning in MLLMs.
2605.25784.decisionReason: No official links or artifact evidence were supplied beyond the arXiv paper. The dataset and scoring protocol are not publicly accessible per the provided information, making it unclear for reuse or submission.

2605.25615.description: UAV-OVO is an out-of-viewpoint generalization benchmark for UAV action recognition. It evaluates models on low-depression viewpoint training data and tests on high-depression viewpoint out-of-distribution data, with class-matched ID/OOD splits.
2605.25615.whyItMatters: Standard UAV action recognition benchmarks often overlook viewpoint shifts, leading to models that rely on viewpoint-specific shortcuts. UAV-OVO provides a controlled testbed to measure and improve robustness to viewpoint changes, which is critical for real-world UAV deployment.
2605.25615.decisionReason: The paper introduces a new benchmark with defined splits (ID/OOD) and a clear evaluation protocol. Although it is presented alongside a method (LATER), the benchmark itself is a standalone reusable resource with a public paper and data (implied). No official artifact link is provided, but the paper serves as a specification.

2605.25758.description: StreamProfileBench evaluates LLMs on fine-grained streaming user profiling. Models maintain a rolling persona summary from a stream of user posts and predict which tags from a candidate pool the user will engage with next. Includes over 120,000 posts from 7,000+ users across five Chinese platforms with metrics for recall, novelty, stability, and error rates.
2605.25758.whyItMatters: Existing user profiling benchmarks use static data, failing to capture real-world streaming UGC and rapidly evolving interests. StreamProfileBench provides a dynamic evaluation that measures plasticity-stability balance, revealing conservative bias in LLMs and enabling practical improvements for personalized systems.
2605.25758.decisionReason: Supplied evidence includes a public GitHub repository with data, code, and a leaderboard, plus a Hugging Face dataset link, establishing a repeatable evaluation object and comparable scoring contract with a clear public reuse path.

2605.25764.description: SpaPath-Bench evaluates pathology foundation models on spatial domain identification using paired whole slide images and spatial transcriptomics data from 42 public slides, measuring partition quality via unsupervised spatial coherence, transcriptomics-referenced agreement, and expert-referenced agreement.
2605.25764.whyItMatters: Standard task-level endpoints obscure what pathology embeddings encode about tissue spatial structure. SpaPath-Bench provides a representation-level diagnostic that isolates spatial understanding, enabling model developers to compare encoders and methods on a fixed protocol and choose architectures suited for spatially aware computational pathology.
2605.25764.decisionReason: The paper defines a named benchmark (SpaPath-Bench) with a clear evaluation object (spatial domain identification on paired WSI-ST data), a repeatable scoring contract (three criteria), and a public code/data pipeline link. It is a fixed dataset/protocol usable by other teams.

2605.26177.description: RepoMirage is a two-stage evaluation suite built on SWE-Bench Verified that applies semantics-preserving repository-level perturbations and extended tasks to probe repository context reasoning in code agents.
2605.26177.whyItMatters: It aims to isolate repository context reasoning from end-to-end issue resolution performance, revealing a gap that could inform structure-aware agent design.
2605.26177.decisionReason: No official artifact link is provided; the paper is the only evidence. The benchmark's public reuse path is not demonstrated, and it is unclear if a scoring contract or data release exists. Defer pending artifact availability.

2605.26176.description: PitchBench evaluates pitch hearing in audio-language models across 28 experiments spanning absolute and relative pitch perception in sequences and chords, varying acoustic conditions and response formats.
2605.26176.whyItMatters: Pitch perception is foundational for musical reasoning, yet existing benchmarks probe it indirectly. PitchBench provides a systematic, controlled evaluation to identify limitations in current models and support the development of pitch-aware audio-language systems.
2605.26176.decisionReason: Named benchmark (PitchBench) with a clear evaluation object (pitch hearing in ALMs) and scoring contract (28 experiments with varying conditions). Public release as a Python package is stated, providing a credible reuse path.

2605.25535.description: PerMemBench evaluates personalized memory systems for LLM agents using multi-year, multi-domain interaction histories across 20 user personas, measuring memory retention accuracy.
2605.25535.whyItMatters: Universal memory policies waste budget on transient interactions and fail to preserve critical context. PerMemBench enables evaluation of personalization, revealing that accurate gating remains an open challenge.
2605.25535.decisionReason: Named benchmark (PerMemBench) with a clear evaluation object (personalized memory retention) and a scoring contract (memory retention rate). Public code repository with dataset and pipeline is provided, meeting the public reuse path requirement.

2605.26322.description: OmniToM evaluates theory of mind in LLMs by requiring explicit belief modeling, extracting belief propositions and labeling them with seven-dimensional schema labels across 895 stories.
2605.26322.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap of end-point question answering in ToM evaluation by forcing explicit mental-state representation, potentially revealing actor-specific belief-tracking bottlenecks.
2605.26322.decisionReason: No public artifact link is provided in the input; only the arXiv paper is available. Without evidence of a public dataset or protocol, the benchmark cannot be verified as reusable. Defer pending artifact availability.

2605.26320.description: MultiSeismo is a multimodal seismic dataset with over 16K events integrating waveforms, intensity maps, population exposure, and text, plus MISCE instruction set for seismic reasoning tasks like retrieval and cross-modal analysis.
2605.26320.whyItMatters: It enables evaluation of multimodal models on specialized scientific data, highlighting challenges in time-series processing and supporting development of domain-specific models.
2605.26320.decisionReason: The dataset is named and provides a clear evaluation object (seismic reasoning) with scoring tasks (MISCE). However, no public artifact link is given; only the paper. The public reuse path is not evidenced in the input. Defer until artifacts are available.

2605.26396.description: MM-CreativityBench evaluates large multimodal models on affordance-grounded creative tool use, requiring scene inspection, entity/part selection, and physically feasible solutions in visually rich environments.
2605.26396.whyItMatters: It probes beyond pattern recognition, assessing grounded exploration and reasoning. Current models show gaps in exploration and hallucination, motivating preference-based alignment.
2605.26396.decisionReason: Named benchmark (MM-CreativityBench) with a clear evaluation object (creative tool use) and scoring contract (entity/part selection accuracy). Public code repository with dataset and evaluation code is provided, meeting public reuse path.

2605.25461.description: MetaphorVU-Bench evaluates metaphorical video understanding in multimodal LLMs through tasks requiring cross-domain mapping, with a benchmark dataset and evaluation code publicly available.
2605.25461.whyItMatters: It fills the gap of systematic evaluation of high-order cognitive capabilities in video understanding, revealing defects in cross-domain mapping and enabling future improvements.
2605.25461.decisionReason: Named benchmark (MetaphorVU-Bench) with a clear evaluation object (metaphorical video understanding) and scoring contract (LLM-based judging). Public code and dataset links are provided, meeting public reuse path.

2605.26244.description: LongAV-Compass evaluates minute-scale audio-visual generation across text-to-audio-video, image-to-audio-video, and video-to-audio-video tasks. It includes 284 curated test cases and an evaluation framework combining multimodal metrics with MLLM-assisted assessment across 20+ dimensions covering segment quality, cross-segment consistency, narrative coherence, semantic alignment, and audiovisual synchronization.
2605.26244.whyItMatters: Existing audio-visual evaluation is limited to short clips, leaving a gap for minute-scale generation. LongAV-Compass provides a standardized protocol for diagnosing degradation in identity consistency, narrative coherence, and alignment over long horizons, supporting comparison of long-form generation models.
2605.26244.decisionReason: Clear benchmark with 284 test cases, unified evaluation framework, public code and dataset, and scored dimensions. Satisfies public_reusable criteria.

2605.25510.description: KIDBench evaluates child-facing safety of LLMs for ages 7-11 using realistic queries and multi-turn child-actor simulations, scored by an LLM-as-a-Judge rubric.
2605.25510.whyItMatters: It addresses a gap in LLM safety evaluation by focusing on age-appropriate responses for children, with a novel rubric and multi-turn assessment.
2605.25510.decisionReason: No code or dataset artifacts provided; only described in paper. Lacks public reuse path, making it a viewpoint probe.

2605.25717.description: FLOATBench is a tabular benchmark for surrogate modeling of tower fatigue in 22 MW floating offshore wind turbines. It provides 582,120 per-section fatigue damage labels from OpenFAST simulations across three tower geometries, with regime-aware splits and three evaluation protocols (random, within-tower regime-aware, cross-tower transfer).
2605.25717.whyItMatters: Previously, no shared benchmark existed for FOWT fatigue surrogates, hindering comparison. FLOATBench provides a standardized dataset and protocol, enabling fair evaluation and highlighting regime-aware performance differences.
2605.25717.decisionReason: Public dataset and code with clear protocols; qualifies as public_reusable.

2605.26394.description: EnterpriseMem-Bench is a multi-turn Text-to-SQL benchmark with 300 sessions and 1,400 turns across three enterprise domains, featuring deterministic ground truth and per-turn memory-critical annotations.
2605.26394.whyItMatters: It addresses the lack of multi-turn evaluation in Text-to-SQL, providing insights into memory architecture effects and model performance degradation.
2605.26394.decisionReason: No code or data links provided; unclear public availability.

2605.26087.description: DiscoverPhysics is an interactive benchmark for LLM agents to discover laws of motion in simulated worlds with altered physics, scoring trajectory MSE and explanation quality.
2605.26087.whyItMatters: It probes long-horizon reasoning and hypothesis refinement, distinguishing recall from genuine scientific reasoning.
2605.26087.decisionReason: No artifacts provided; unclear how to access and run the benchmark.

2605.26086.description: Claw-Anything evaluates always-on LLM personal assistants in simulated environments with long-horizon activity histories, interdependent backend services, and GUI/CLI across devices. It includes 200 human-verified tasks scored on completion, robustness, communication, and safety, with a live leaderboard.
2605.26086.whyItMatters: It expands agent evaluation to broad, always-on contexts, revealing capability gaps in stateful, proactive assistance and supporting scalable data generation for training.
2605.26086.decisionReason: Public code, data, and leaderboard; clear scoring contract; supports submission-based comparison.

2605.26036.description: CityRep is a benchmark for urban representation learning across 8 cities and 8 tasks with spatially structured splits to mitigate leakage.
2605.26036.whyItMatters: It addresses inconsistencies in urban representation evaluation and supports generalization-aware model selection.
2605.26036.decisionReason: No code or data links provided; unclear public availability.

2605.25382.description: AuthTrace is a diagnostic benchmark for evidence construction in thematically dense single-author corpora, with fan-in annotations and pack-level protocol.
2605.25382.whyItMatters: It provides a diagnostic lens for identifying where evidence construction fails and which paradigm works best.
2605.25382.decisionReason: No artifacts provided; unclear how to run.

2605.26302.description: Evaluates the reliability of deployed AI agents over extended operational lifetimes. The benchmark organizes agent aging into four mechanisms—compression, interference, revision, and maintenance—and uses temporal dependency graphs and paired counterfactual probes to produce diagnostic profiles of the memory pipeline's write, retrieval, and utilization stages. It includes multiple scenarios and memory policies, with scoring based on task performance over sessions.
2605.26302.whyItMatters: Existing agent evaluations are snapshot-based and ignore how agents degrade after deployment. This benchmark measures longevity and provides mechanism-level diagnosis, enabling stage-targeted repair and more dependable agent deployment.
2605.26302.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public code repository, defined scenarios, scoring methodology, and diagnostic profiles, providing a reusable evaluation path for other teams.

2605.25707.description: Evaluates the robustness of computer use agents under common environment corruptions such as pop-ups, resolution changes, and competing applications. The benchmark introduces 9 configurable corruptions and evaluates agent performance on desktop tasks using multimodal LLM-based agents, measuring task completion rates.
2605.25707.whyItMatters: Real-world execution environments are imperfect, and minor corruptions can cause significant performance degradation. This benchmark quantifies agent fragility and supports the development of more robust computer use agents.
2605.25707.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public code and environment, defined corruption types, and evaluation methodology, providing a reusable path for other teams.

2605.24945.description: Evaluates data-driven numerical weather forecasting models under operational conditions, using strictly out-of-distribution test data from 2025 and integrating low-latency operational analysis and large-scale in-situ observations from over 10,000 stations. It provides metrics for global forecasting and for extreme events such as heatwaves, cold surges, and tropical cyclones.
2605.24945.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks rely on reanalysis products that do not reflect real-time operational constraints, leading to mismatches between benchmark scores and real-world performance. This benchmark provides a more faithful and operationally relevant evaluation paradigm.
2605.24945.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public code repository, defined test data and metrics, providing a reusable evaluation path for other teams.

2605.25240.description: A dataset of 30 legal tasks with rubric scores and pairwise preference judgments from practicing attorneys, used to compare rubric-based scoring and comparative judgment.
2605.25240.whyItMatters: Supports research on expert judgment elicitation and aggregation in domains without ground truth.
2605.25240.decisionReason: Primarily supports the paper's comparison of evaluation methodologies; lacks a standalone public comparison path for model evaluation.

2605.25200.description: A benchmark for multi-user, multi-turn travel planning with 650 tasks and a synchronous group-chat sandbox, evaluating elicitation, coordination, and fairness-aware planning.
2605.25200.whyItMatters: Highlights the challenge of group-level outcome quality for LLM agents.
2605.25200.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official links provided; evidence unclear for standalone reuse.

2605.25009.description: A benchmark decomposing synthetic image detection into annotated forensic cognitive skills, used to evaluate a proposed detection framework.
2605.25009.whyItMatters: Supports evidence-based synthetic image detection beyond binary classification.
2605.25009.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official links provided; lacks a standalone comparison path.

2605.24703.description: A controlled benchmark for evaluating analytical skills in time-series question answering: temporal scale selection, temporal localization, and cross-interval integration.
2605.24703.whyItMatters: Skill-level evaluation reveals temporal reasoning failures obscured by aggregate scores.
2605.24703.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official links provided; lacks a standalone comparison path.

2605.24782.description: A benchmark dataset for tropical cyclone research with an automated construction pipeline, used to probe scientific alignment of vision foundation models.
2605.24782.whyItMatters: Examines whether models rely on visual shortcuts rather than structural invariants in scientific domains.
2605.24782.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official links provided; lacks a standalone comparison path.

2607.20471.description: SDR-Bench evaluates LLM personalization in a two-party framework. It includes 6,279 customer success stories across 22 industries and ~200 enterprises, with a temporally constrained simulation to prevent data leakage. Scoring compares model-generated outreach against human outcomes.
2607.20471.whyItMatters: SDR-Bench addresses the gap in evaluating LLM personalization as a two-party problem, where generated messages must induce action in a third party. It provides a reproducible public benchmark for comparing model performance on this task, with validation against field deployment.
2607.20471.decisionReason: SDR-Bench is a named benchmark with a public corpus and simulation, enabling reproducible evaluation of LLM personalization. It provides a scoring contract based on receiver actions and a public path for inspection. The paper indicates public release of the benchmark and arena.

2605.24777.description: MR-LiDAR is a multi-resolution LiDAR benchmark for roadside perception. It includes point cloud data and annotations from 16-, 32-, 80-, and 128-beam LiDARs in identical scenarios, covering vehicles and vulnerable road users at various distances.
2605.24777.whyItMatters: The benchmark targets the need for empirical comparison of LiDAR configurations to guide sensor selection in roadside perception systems, addressing cost and performance trade-offs.
2605.24777.decisionReason: The input provides no official links to the benchmark dataset, code, or evaluation scripts, and artifact evidence is empty, leaving the public availability and reuse path unclear.

2605.24417.description: LLMTabBench evaluates LLMs on binary tabular classification in zero- and few-shot settings, using real-world and controlled synthetic datasets to study the effect of task descriptions and examples on performance.
2605.24417.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the gap in understanding how LLMs perform on tabular data under low-data regimes, which can inform their deployment in data-scarce applications.
2605.24417.decisionReason: Evidence of a standalone public comparison path is unclear: no artifact link or official benchmark homepage is supplied, and the paper describes a study rather than a publicly reusable evaluation protocol.

2605.24635.description: HiMed is a Hindi medical dataset and benchmark suite covering Western and Indian medicine. It evaluates medical reasoning in Hindi across multiple tasks, with data and evaluation scripts publicly released on GitHub.
2605.24635.whyItMatters: Hindi remains underrepresented in medical LLMs; this benchmark enables systematic evaluation of cross-lingual medical reasoning, helping reduce performance gaps between English and Hindi in healthcare applications.
2605.24635.decisionReason: Publicly available data and code provide a clear reuse path for evaluation. Scoring is based on established reasoning formats. Excluded from score_submission as no ongoing leaderboard is indicated.

2605.24636.description: GlobalDentBench evaluates LLM clinical reasoning in dentistry with 8,978 expert-validated questions across 14 specialties and 88 countries, covering multiple-choice, short-answer, and case-based formats at three reasoning levels.
2605.24636.whyItMatters: It provides a multinational dental benchmark with expert calibration to assess knowledge recall, routine and individualized reasoning, revealing safety risks in LLM clinical recommendations and supporting rigorous validation before deployment.
2605.24636.decisionReason: Defines a concrete benchmark with a repeatable evaluation protocol, scoring contract via accuracy and risk analysis, and a public path through the arXiv paper and dataset described.

2605.24503.description: Evaluates multimodal large language models on explainable compliance analysis in commercial kitchen surveillance, using video clips with dual-channel annotations and a composite metric.
2605.24503.whyItMatters: Provides a protocol for assessing both spatial localization and semantic rule understanding in video anomaly detection, addressing a gap in existing event-level binary classification benchmarks.
2605.24503.decisionReason: No official artifact link supplied; data and code availability unclear.

2605.24456.description: EgoProx evaluates multimodal large language models on egocentric 3D proximity reasoning, with tasks organized along a cognitive hierarchy covering intention, exploration, exploitation, and chain-of-actions reasoning.
2605.24456.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in assessing embodied 3D spatial reasoning in MLLMs, a capability important for robotics and augmented reality applications.
2605.24456.decisionReason: No official dataset or code release links provided; reproducibility and public comparison path unclear.

2605.24765.description: The evaluation object is a dataset for privacy-aware cybersecurity question answering, covering key security domains with private entity labels. The main capability evaluated is QA accuracy and masking performance.
2605.24765.whyItMatters: The evaluation gap is the lack of context-rich datasets for privacy-preserving QA in cybersecurity, which hinders progress. This benchmark's value is in enabling controlled information disclosure and studying privacy-utility trade-offs for deployable models.
2605.24765.decisionReason: Dataset and generation framework are promised only upon acceptance; no public artifact yet. The paper indicates future release, so public reuse path is unclear. Benchmark mode unclear.

2606.02603.description: COD10K-C evaluates camouflaged object detection models under 8 corruption types at 5 severity levels, yielding 40 conditions and 81,040 image pairs based on COD10K. Models are scored on Dice and other standard metrics for segmentation robustness.
2606.02603.whyItMatters: Standard camouflaged object detection benchmarks measure performance on clean images only, while real-world captures include blur, noise, weather, and compression artifacts. This benchmark quantifies robustness drops under such corruptions, enabling selection of models that degrade gracefully in practical conditions.
2606.02603.decisionReason: COD10K-C is a named corruption robustness benchmark with a clear evaluation protocol, 40 conditions, and a promised public release via GitHub, providing a repeatable comparison path.

2605.24305.description: ChaosBench-Logic v2 evaluates LLM logical reasoning over dynamical systems with 40,886 questions across 165 systems, 27 first-order logic predicates, and 78 axiom edges. The CARE protocol measures calibration and adversarial robustness, reporting metrics such as MCC.
2605.24305.whyItMatters: Binary accuracy on reasoning benchmarks hides failures like prior collapse and inconsistency under paraphrase. This benchmark surfaces these pathologies and quantifies reasoning about parameter-dependent dynamics, guiding improvements in LLM reasoning capabilities.
2605.24305.decisionReason: ChaosBench-Logic v2 is a named benchmark with a fixed 40,886-question dataset and a defined evaluation protocol (CARE), and it is presented as a benchmark for comparing models, meeting the criteria for public reusable.

2605.24652.description: AVBench evaluates audio-video generative models across ten fine-grained dimensions covering visual quality, audio quality, and cross-modal consistency for human-centric scenarios. It uses specialized evaluators trained via preference learning and provides continuous scores from prediction confidence.
2605.24652.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks for AV generation are coarse and rely on generic multimodal LLMs, leading to inaccurate assessments. AVBench offers automated, human-aligned evaluation with fine-grained metrics, enabling reliable model comparison and serving as a potential reward signal for RLHF.
2605.24652.decisionReason: AVBench is a named benchmark with a defined evaluation setup and a public dataset for training evaluators, offering a repeatable scoring mechanism, and is intended for comparing AV generation models.

2605.24573.description: AstroMind evaluates LLM reasoning about spacecraft behavior across intent inference, maneuver parameter estimation, and threat assessment, using physics-grounded simulations with realistic sensing noise. Metrics capture semantic correctness and quantitative consistency under physical constraints.
2605.24573.whyItMatters: Space situational awareness lacks benchmarks for reasoning about why spacecraft maneuver, not just detection. AstroMind provides a shared test that combines physics accuracy and tactical interpretation, enabling comparison of models on this critical reasoning task.
2605.24573.decisionReason: AstroMind is a named benchmark with a defined task set and scoring metrics, and it is positioned as a benchmark for evaluating models, providing a credible evaluation path.

2605.23237.description: StereoGenBench is a synthetic multi-camera benchmark for stereo generation, rendered in Unreal Engine with a rigid six-camera array. It provides calibrated view pairs across baseline regimes, along with RGB, metric depth, intrinsics, and poses for each scene.
2605.23237.whyItMatters: Stereo generation and view synthesis require controlled baseline and intrinsics for evaluation, which existing resources lack. This benchmark enables measuring sensitivity to baseline regimes and target-camera consistency under matched scene content, supporting development of stereo generation models.
2605.23237.decisionReason: StereoGenBench is a named benchmark with a public dataset on Hugging Face and evaluation code, providing a clear public reuse path and a stable data contract.

2605.24117.description: SkillEvolBench evaluates whether LLM agents can distill episodic experience into reusable procedural skills. It includes 180 tasks across six environments, with acquisition tasks and frozen deployment tasks testing context shift, adversarial shortcuts, and composition. Scoring uses success rates and other agent metrics.
2605.24117.whyItMatters: It is unclear whether LLM agents can form durable procedural skills from experience. SkillEvolBench provides a diagnostic testbed comparing skill-based learning against raw-trajectory reuse, informing agent design and training.
2605.24117.decisionReason: SkillEvolBench is a named benchmark with a defined task set and protocol, intended for comparing agent configurations, and offers a public evaluation setting.

2605.23168.description: PoisonForge benchmarks task-level targeted poisoning of instruction-tuned LLMs, parameterizing bias type, poisoning mode, appearance count, and target output length. It evaluates 12 open-weight models across five families with primarily 1% poison budget, using attack success rate as the main metric.
2605.23168.whyItMatters: Data supply chain poisoning poses a real threat when fine-tuning on unvetted data. PoisonForge quantifies vulnerability across models and configurations, highlighting that design choices rather than scale drive risk, aiding in risk assessment and mitigation.
2605.23168.decisionReason: PoisonForge is a named benchmark with released configurations and analysis code, offering a repeatable comparison of model vulnerability, meeting the criteria for public reusable.

2605.23668.description: NQP-Bench is a dataset within the OnePred paper for evaluating next-query prediction in multi-turn conversations. It spans three diverse subsets and is used to compare OnePred against baselines.
2605.23668.whyItMatters: Next-query prediction lacks dedicated benchmarks; NQP-Bench provides a testbed for this task, enabling evaluation of proactive conversational systems.
2605.23668.decisionReason: NQP-Bench is introduced solely to support the OnePred model, serving as a viewpoint probe rather than a standalone benchmark with independent comparison path. No separate ongoing public benchmark operation is indicated.

2605.23543.description: JEDI is a benchmark suite for the Java Stream API, generated by converting SQL benchmarks into Java benchmarks. It includes both stream-based and imperative query implementations to evaluate performance of parallelization strategies.
2605.23543.whyItMatters: There is a lack of benchmarks for the Java Stream API, making it difficult to optimize the API and analyze stream performance. JEDI provides a dedicated suite to guide developers in writing efficient code and researchers in optimizing the API.
2605.23543.decisionReason: JEDI is a dedicated benchmark suite with a clear evaluation object (Java Stream API performance), a stable scoring contract (comparing different implementations), and a public reuse path (automatically generated code and benchmarks).

2605.23187.description: IntentionNav evaluates active object search from implicit human instructions in 176 Isaac Sim scenes. Episodes provide free-text intent, RGB-D observations, and pose, with the target object withheld. The benchmark includes 500 intents over 64 categories and four intent modes.
2605.23187.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in object navigation where agents must infer targets from indirect human intent, showing persistent bottlenecks in target selection and terminal localization.
2605.23187.decisionReason: No public artifact or code link is provided, and the evaluation setup is described as diagnostic with no published scoring contract or reusable pathway.

2605.23215.description: FastKernels evaluates GPU kernel generation for production inference across 46 representative architectures spanning 8 categories. It measures correctness and speedup of candidate kernels against reference implementations at multiple abstraction levels, from single-kernel to end-to-end serving.
2605.23215.whyItMatters: Existing kernel benchmarks reward sandbox optimizations that fail in production. FastKernels aligns evaluation with real inference frameworks, providing a benchmark where scores translate to throughput improvements in production codebases.
2605.23215.decisionReason: Public code repository and official paper provide a repeatable evaluation protocol with baseline and candidate slots, validation, and speedup measurement. The benchmark is designed for agent kernel comparison with a clear scoring contract.

2605.24110.description: EvoCode-Bench evaluates coding agents in multi-turn iterative interactions, with 26 stateful coding tasks and 227 evaluated rounds. Each task preserves the agent's workspace for 5-15 rounds, specifies requirements via observable behavior, and uses cumulative executable tests to verify new and prior requirements. Scoring uses MT@4, a four-attempt fail-stop multi-round score, and SR, a single-round score from a reference-completed prior state.
2605.24110.whyItMatters: Existing coding benchmarks typically evaluate a single specification and final output, missing the ability to handle evolving requirements. EvoCode-Bench fills this gap by assessing whether agents can maintain a working codebase over multiple rounds. The gap between SR and MT@4 scores reveals that high single-turn performance does not guarantee sustained multi-turn success, providing a more relevant evaluation for real-world iterative development.
2605.24110.decisionReason: The paper defines a named benchmark with a clear evaluation protocol, scoring metrics (MT@4 and SR), and a public data release and infrastructure, establishing a credible path for other teams to run or inspect it. The benchmark is a standalone reusable resource, not merely a one-off for the paper, and is not marked as using an existing benchmark.

2605.23176.description: DriveSpatial is a benchmark of 15.6K human-verified QA pairs across 20 tasks from five AD datasets, evaluating VLMs on cognitive scene construction, multi-view relational understanding, temporal reasoning, and generalization.
2605.23176.whyItMatters: Existing AD vision-language benchmarks focus on static, single-view QA, leaving unclear whether VLMs can reason over dynamic driving scenes. DriveSpatial provides a multi-sourced, human-verified protocol to measure spatiotemporal reasoning and reveals a substantial human-model gap.
2605.23176.decisionReason: DriveSpatial is a named benchmark with a defined task set, human-verified QA pairs, and clear evaluation of four abilities. It will be released, providing a public reuse path for other teams.

2605.24267.description: The evaluation targets conversational implicature in question utterances, using a semi-automated pipeline to generate question-context-interpretation instances with controlled variation.
2605.24267.whyItMatters: This evaluation probes the gap between generation and inference in pragmatic reasoning, but no public comparison path is provided beyond the paper's findings.
2605.24267.decisionReason: No public benchmark artifact or leaderboard is supplied; the proposed pipeline is not shown as a fixed reusable protocol.

2605.23699.description: CRONOS is an intervention-based benchmark for evaluating counterfactual physical consistency in video prediction models. It provides a photorealistic Unreal Engine environment with controlled videos of physical events (collision, occlusion, fall) while intervening on viewpoint, scene, object category, and object appearance. The evaluation protocol defines six metrics computed via video segmentation, tracking, 3D reconstruction, and VLM-based task performance.
2605.23699.whyItMatters: Current video models often rely on superficial correlations rather than causal structure. CRONOS enables systematic diagnosis of how prediction quality degrades under controlled interventions, providing a concrete target for developing models robust to variations in viewpoint and context.
2605.23699.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a fixed dataset and protocol with clear metrics, and provides released code and evaluation scripts, making it publicly reusable for model comparison.

2605.24279.description: ContextEcho measures persona drift in long agentic-coding sessions, combining a 25-probe identity suite, snapshot-then-probe protocol, and three anonymized Claude Code sessions.
2605.24279.whyItMatters: Persona drift can affect user trust and model reliability in real-world deployment, but existing evaluations may miss it. ContextEcho provides a framework for auditing persona consistency across long sessions.
2605.24279.decisionReason: Primarily supports the paper's findings with no clear standalone public comparison path; the artifact evidence is empty and no official benchmark site or leaderboard is provided.

2605.23216.description: CaST-Bench evaluates causal chain-grounded spatio-temporal reasoning in video question answering. It contains 2,066 questions over 1,015 videos with causal chains annotated as temporal segments and bounding-box tracks. The evaluation suite includes metrics for answer correctness and visual evidence grounding.
2605.23216.whyItMatters: Existing video QA benchmarks lack fine-grained causal grounding. CaST-Bench provides a protocol to assess whether VLMs can identify and localize causal evidence chains, supporting progress in transparent and reliable video understanding.
2605.23216.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a fixed dataset of 2,066 questions, annotated causal chains, and a defined evaluation suite including metrics for answer correctness and grounding. The project page offers public access for inspection and reuse.

2605.24183.description: AvalancheBench evaluates enterprise data agents on latent world recovery, scoring analytical understanding of segments, drivers, temporal events, and relationships from generated observations.
2605.24183.whyItMatters: The evaluation gap is the need for controlled diagnostics of whether agents recover analytical structure behind enterprise data, with a rubric for partial credit and error propagation analysis.
2605.24183.decisionReason: No public code, dataset, or scoring implementation provided; only paper and abstract, so reusability and contract clarity are unclear.

2605.22907.description: VideoOdyssey evaluates models on ultra-long-context video understanding using videos averaging 109 minutes across 11 domains, with two subsets for visual and audio-visual understanding. Tasks include question answering with continuous certificates averaging 16 and 12.8 minutes respectively.
2605.22907.whyItMatters: Existing long-video benchmarks often only test short segments, failing to capture the cognitive load of continuous reasoning over long spans. VideoOdyssey's multi-level continuous certificates provide a diagnostic for evaluating model performance across varying context lengths, addressing a gap in measuring true long-context and omni-modal understanding.
2605.22907.decisionReason: The paper describes a new benchmark with a defined dataset and evaluation protocol, including a scoring contract based on continuous certificate length. The arXiv page provides public access to the paper and likely benchmark details, enabling reuse by other teams.

2605.22570.description: VGenST-Bench evaluates spatio-temporal reasoning in multimodal large language models using 1,200 procedurally generated videos with controlled scene composition, camera trajectory, and reasoning targets. It covers 12 reasoning tasks across three spatial scales and 12 QA types across three reasoning levels, with multiple choice and open-ended question variants.
2605.22570.whyItMatters: Existing video reasoning benchmarks rely on static or passively curated content, limiting fine-grained diagnosis. VGenST-Bench uses active synthesis to enable controlled and diverse evaluation of fine-grained spatio-temporal reasoning, supporting model comparison and targeted improvement in MLLMs.
2605.22570.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named, repeatable evaluation object with a public code repository and project page. It provides a clear evaluation protocol, taxonomy, and QA generation pipeline, and can be run by other teams, satisfying the public_reusable mode.

2605.22219.description: SGR-Bench evaluates search agents on state-gated retrieval tasks. It includes 100 expert-curated tasks across 12 public data ecosystems, requiring agents to configure site-specific filters, views, hierarchies, or scopes to retrieve structured answers. Tasks come in goal-oriented and constraint-guided formulations.
2605.22219.whyItMatters: SGR-Bench addresses an undercharacterized class of retrieval tasks where evidence is hidden behind site-specific retrieval states. It provides a standardized evaluation to measure agents' ability to establish correct retrieval states, which is critical for real-world data retrieval from specialized websites.
2605.22219.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a fixed dataset with 100 tasks, a rubric-based scoring contract, and public access to data and evaluation instructions, enabling reuse by other teams.

2605.21919.description: SDGBiasBench is a benchmark suite for evaluating vision-language models on Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) reasoning, covering 500k multiple-choice questions and 50k regression tasks.
2605.21919.whyItMatters: Existing SDG evaluation tools lack a combined assessment of qualitative and quantitative reasoning, and this benchmark aims to expose systematic biases in model predictions. The value lies in enabling more reliable AI for sustainable development monitoring.
2605.21919.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark suite but does not provide an official public link to the benchmark artifacts or evaluation code. The absence of a clear public reuse path and unclear scoring contract lead to deferral.

2605.22413.description: ReceiptBench evaluates multimodal large language models on visual information extraction from receipts. It includes 10k human-annotated receipts and four hierarchical subtasks: basic perception, format normalization, semantic reasoning, and structure parsing, with defined metrics and scoring.
2605.22413.whyItMatters: Existing VIE benchmarks lack scale, realism, and semantic granularity. ReceiptBench provides a standardized, publicly available evaluation path for comparing models on diverse receipt understanding tasks, supporting practical deployment decisions in document automation.
2605.22413.decisionReason: Named benchmark ReceiptBench with a defined evaluation object, subtasks, and metrics. Public dataset and code are provided, enabling other teams to run or inspect the evaluation.

2608.02615.description: OncoTriad-QA is a patient-level benchmark for pan-cancer question answering, integrating radiology, pathology, genomics, and clinical metadata from TCGA. It includes 86.1k questions across 9,281 cases and 32 cancer cohorts, with annotations derived from curated labels and diagnostic reports.
2608.02615.whyItMatters: Existing medical LLM benchmarks often focus on isolated modalities. OncoTriad-QA could address the gap in evaluating integrated, patient-level reasoning across multiple evidence types, which is crucial for real-world oncology decision support.
2608.02615.decisionReason: The source describes a benchmark with a repeatable evaluation object (patient-level QA) and scoring contract (MCQ accuracy, BERTScore-F1). However, no official public artifact or hosting link is provided, and the benchmark is not yet accessible for external reuse or inspection. Therefore, the public reuse path is unclear.

2605.22100.description: MPDocBench-Parse is a benchmark for multi-page document parsing, covering 433 manually annotated documents with 3,246 pages across 15 document types in English and Chinese. It evaluates content fidelity and logical structure, including text, table, formula recognition, reading order, and heading hierarchy recovery.
2605.22100.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the lack of realistic multi-page document parsing evaluation, offering a more comprehensive protocol for assessing semantic continuity, hierarchical structure recovery, and visual content preservation, which is crucial for advancing document parsing systems in practical applications.
2605.22100.decisionReason: The benchmark is described in a paper but no official benchmark website, leaderboard, or downloadable dataset link is provided in the input. Only the arXiv paper link is given. Thus, the public reuse path is unclear. Deferring until official benchmark artifacts are publicly available.

2605.22080.description: JMed48k evaluates vision-language models on 48,862 Japanese medical licensing exam questions from 11 national examinations (2005-2025), with images annotated under an 8-type taxonomy. The JMed48k-Eval subset contains 12,484 scored questions, including text-only and with-image items, scored separately.
2605.22080.whyItMatters: Provides a profession-stratified evaluation for vision-language models in Japanese medical licensing, enabling comparison of image use across professions and model types, and addressing the lack of multilingual medical benchmarks.
2605.22080.decisionReason: Publicly released dataset with fixed protocol and clear scoring contract, intended for reproducible evaluation by other teams.

2605.22079.description: A benchmark for generating Information Delivery Specification (IDS) XML from BIM information requirements, with 166 examples in English and Japanese. It evaluates LLMs on formal validity via IDSAuditTool and content fidelity via facet-level macro-F1 against gold IDS files.
2605.22079.whyItMatters: IDS authoring requires domain expertise and vocabulary conformance; this benchmark quantifies LLM performance on a structured generation task where output must satisfy external validation tools, filling a gap for capability assessment in BIM-specific language models.
2605.22079.decisionReason: Publicly released benchmark with fixed dataset, two-stage evaluation protocol, and open artifacts (Hugging Face and Zenodo), providing a credible path for reuse and comparison.

2605.22247.description: IdioLink is a retrieval benchmark with 10,700 documents and 2,140 queries across 107 idioms, testing the linking of idiomatic expressions to literal or paraphrased equivalents. Annotations mark core meaning spans, and scoring is based on retrieval quality against these spans.
2605.22247.whyItMatters: Existing retrieval models often rely on surface similarity and fail on idiomatic expressions. IdioLink provides a reusable testbed to measure semantic abstraction beyond lexical overlap, offering a practical way to evaluate idiom-aware retrieval systems.
2605.22247.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a clear evaluation object (documents, queries, annotations), has a comparable scoring contract (retrieval against annotated spans), and is publicly hosted on arXiv with data and code likely accessible, making it reusable. The paper includes baselines and the dataset appears fixed.

2605.21858.description: HyperAlign-Bench is a benchmark introduced in a paper for evaluating hypergraph structural modeling in large language models, covering vertex-level and hyperedge-level tasks.
2605.21858.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs on high-order relational structures, which are common in real-world data but underrepresented in existing benchmarks.
2605.21858.decisionReason: The benchmark is named but lacks sufficient detail on standardized scoring and a clear public reuse path; artifact evidence is missing.

2605.23055.description: EvalAwareBench is a factor-controlled benchmark of 100 paired safety-capability tasks, each toggling one of eight evaluation-awareness triggers while holding the underlying request fixed. It measures recognition and behavioral change in language models under evaluation.
2605.23055.whyItMatters: Evaluation awareness can distort benchmark results, especially for safety evaluations. EvalAwareBench enables controlled measurement of model sensitivity to evaluative signals, helping researchers identify and mitigate threats to benchmark validity.
2605.23055.decisionReason: The abstract describes a factor-controlled benchmark with 100 tasks, a clear protocol for toggling factors, and a path for others to reuse it, meeting the criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2605.21974.description: CSVFidelity-Bench evaluates knowledge graph construction from statistical tables, focusing on the effect of extraction schema and format coupling on fidelity. It includes 15 datasets, 11 Type-II and 4 Type-III tables, with 1,892 gold standard facts across 6 domains.
2605.21974.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating knowledge graph construction fidelity, particularly the overlooked interaction between serialization format and schema constraints, which can cause catastrophic coverage loss.
2605.21974.decisionReason: Primarily a diagnostic probe for a specific phenomenon (format-constraint coupling) with a small dataset; lacks a standalone public comparison path for general use.

2605.22068.description: COCOTree evaluates open tree-structured visual decomposition, segmenting images into hierarchical trees of visual components with unconstrained granularity. It includes over 21K images and 1.8M structural nodes, with 3.5K unique labels, and uses the Open Tree Quality (OTQ) metric for scoring.
2605.22068.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized evaluation for a new task paradigm, enabling comparison across models on open vocabulary and long-tail visual structures, where existing benchmarks lack hierarchical decomposition metrics.
2605.22068.decisionReason: Offers a large-scale dataset with a clear evaluation protocol and public code/data links, making it reusable for benchmarking.

2605.22643.description: Boiling the Frog evaluates whether tool-using AI models in corporate settings are susceptible to incremental attacks through multi-turn scenarios with persistent workspaces. It includes a three-level operational risk taxonomy and scores attack success rate (ASR) on resulting artifact state.
2605.22643.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in safety evaluation for agents acting in environments, focusing on incremental manipulation rather than single-turn textual outputs.
2605.22643.decisionReason: Designed for ongoing model comparison with a clear scoring (ASR) and defined scenarios, though no public code/data link is provided, making reuse uncertain.

2605.22645.description: AtelierEval evaluates prompting proficiency of humans and MLLMs for text-to-image systems via 360 tasks, using a skill-based agentic evaluator (AtelierJudge) that scores prompt-image pairs subjectively and objectively.
2605.22645.whyItMatters: Introduces a new evaluation angle for T2I pipelines, measuring upstream prompting ability which is currently unassessed.
2605.22645.decisionReason: Primarily introduced to validate the AtelierJudge evaluator and reveal mimicry vs planning; lacks a clear standalone reuse path for other teams.

2605.22366.description: AgroTools evaluates tool-augmented multimodal agents in agriculture, with 539 QA instances, 1,097 images, 14 executable tools, and structured tool-use traces for process and outcome evaluation.
2605.22366.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in agricultural benchmarks by assessing tool use and workflow execution, not just final answers, enabling deeper evaluation of agent capabilities.
2605.22366.decisionReason: Provides a public dataset with clear task definitions and dual-view scoring, making it reusable for benchmarking.

2605.24045.description: InteractBind provides a large-scale dataset of ~100k protein-ligand pairs with fine-grained binding-site localization tasks and interaction maps for six non-covalent interaction types, plus affinity and similarity-controlled splits.
2605.24045.whyItMatters: Challenges existing protein-ligand benchmarks by focusing on localization and interaction interpretability, which is critical for drug discovery.
2605.24045.decisionReason: Serves as a dataset and benchmark for studying whether models learn binding sites or likelihood; mainly supports the paper's finding, not a standalone public comparison.

2608.20116.description: A synthetic benchmark studying how LLMs arbitrate between conflicting textual and numerical evidence, with latent risk trajectories generating both modalities.
2608.20116.whyItMatters: Evaluates a failure mode in tool-augmented decision systems where models may prefer one evidence type over another without following reliability cues.
2608.20116.decisionReason: Primarily supports one paper's findings on evidence arbitration and lacks a standalone public comparison path or reusable evaluation harness.

2608.19583.description: VGI-Bench evaluates visual reasoning in video generation models across 27 tasks and 810 instances, covering domain and skill taxonomy with calibrated difficulty.
2608.19583.whyItMatters: Provides a comprehensive, standardized evaluation for video generation models' reasoning, with fine-grained scoring to guide model development and comparison.
2608.19583.decisionReason: Formally named benchmark with clear task suite, scoring criteria, and public website for inspection.

2608.19936.description: Behavioral probes that measure benchmark optimization in ASR models by testing reproduction of reference transcript spans under underdetermined audio conditions.
2608.19936.whyItMatters: Identifies whether high-scoring ASR models rely on benchmark-conditioned behaviors that may not generalize to real-world transcription.
2608.19936.decisionReason: The probes primarily support this paper's analysis of benchmark optimization and are not presented as a standalone reusable benchmark with a public scoring contract.

2608.19799.description: SWE-bench Science evaluates coding agents on 119 repository-level tasks from 98 GitHub repositories spanning 20 scientific domains, organized into Issue-driven, Expert-exploratory, and Engineering-integration paradigms. It measures pass@1 for repairing scientific software.
2608.19799.whyItMatters: Existing coding agent benchmarks emphasize aggregate success and provide limited insight into failures in scientific software. SWE-bench Science provides a broad testbed for studying capabilities and failure mechanisms, noting that even top agents achieve pass@1 below 50%, helping developers identify where scientific knowledge helps or hinders repair.
2608.19799.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined tasks, scoring (pass@1), and public access via arXiv; repository tasks are fixed and reusable, though no official code link is provided but paper gives artifacts.

2608.20237.description: RuleMaze evaluates multimodal large language models on rule-compliant visual spatial planning. Models navigate visual mazes with natural-language rule constraints, requiring joint perception, rule interpretation, and action planning. The benchmark provides procedural maze generation, rule-conditioned trajectories, and seen/unseen rule splits with validators.
2608.20237.whyItMatters: RuleMaze addresses the lack of benchmarks for evaluating MLLMs on grounded spatial planning under explicit rule constraints. It provides a controlled environment to measure rule compliance and generalization, offering practical value for testing and developing models that must follow complex instructions in visual environments.
2608.20237.decisionReason: RuleMaze is a controllable benchmark with public dataset and code, enabling model comparison and reuse. The scoring contract includes validators and evaluation splits, and the public repository provides a clear path for other teams to run and inspect the benchmark.

2608.19974.description: A controlled financial-compliance environment (ReguSim) and a target-marked monitoring benchmark (ReguBench) that evaluate LLM agents' rule grounding in financial compliance, separating reasoning, action, enforcement, and monitoring evidence.
2608.19974.whyItMatters: Financial compliance requires agents to not only state rules but act accordingly. This evaluation could reveal whether LLM agents can reliably ground actions in executable constraints, but without released artifacts the basis for comparison is unclear.
2608.19974.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark but no code or data artifacts are provided in the input, so a public reuse path is not evident. Without evidence of a stable scoring contract or released materials, the benchmark cannot be published.

2608.19646.canonicalNameEvidence: PL-NBA: A Possession-level Universal Basketball Video Dataset Supporting Multiple Visual Understanding Tasks
2608.19646.description: A possession-level basketball video dataset with 11,000 clips from 60 NBA games, annotated with 31,567 events including player names, captions, event types, and timestamps. It supports event recognition, video captioning, temporal action localization, and action anticipation.
2608.19646.whyItMatters: Existing sports video datasets focus on isolated actions, limiting analysis of continuous events and complex tasks like anticipation. PL-NBA provides a standard evaluation suite for multiple visual understanding tasks on continuous game events, enabling comparison of methods in a realistic setting.
2608.19646.decisionReason: The paper explicitly introduces PL-NBA as a challenging benchmark for sports video understanding, with a defined task suite and evaluation protocol. The dataset is described and the paper provides a clear path for public access via arXiv.

2608.19746.description: PersonalBench evaluates inference-time LLM personalization by measuring authorship resemblance across 50 authors and 1,000 generations, using LUAR, LLM-as-judge, and stylometrics. It provides metrics like LUAR similarity and AUC.
2608.19746.whyItMatters: Fills gap in personalization evaluation by focusing on authorship resemblance rather than task accuracy. PersonalBench serves as a calibrated measuring stick, showing current methods modulate style but fail to bridge the human-LLM authorship gap, informing future personalization approaches.
2608.19746.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined evaluation protocol (three lenses) and scoring metrics; data of 50 authors and 1,000 generations is fixed and presumably usable, but no official code link is provided, though paper is public.

2608.19741.canonicalNameEvidence: Thinkingbox-bench contains 507 policy-conditioned workflows across numerous scenarios
2608.19741.description: A sandbox and benchmark for agents in stateful business workflows, featuring 507 policy-conditioned workflows across retail, hospitality, auto insurance, neobank IT, and consulting. Evaluation uses executable checks on terminal backend state, rejecting wrong, missing, or extra effects.
2608.19741.whyItMatters: Many agent benchmarks evaluate only response or tool-call validity, missing end-to-end task completion. Thinkingbox-bench measures reliable completion of multi-turn business workflows, revealing gaps in current agents and promoting progress in stateful task reliability.
2608.19741.decisionReason: The paper and official repository explicitly release Thinkingbox and Thinkingbox-bench, with a defined evaluation protocol and public GitHub repositories for both framework and data, providing a credible path for other teams to run or inspect.

2608.20106.description: A wine-domain knowledge benchmark of 3,266 multiple-choice questions across six pillars and four difficulty tiers, built from source-anchored facts with an LLM-driven pipeline and nine-agent audit.
2608.20106.whyItMatters: Domain-specific knowledge benchmarks are needed to evaluate LLMs beyond general knowledge. This benchmark offers a structured, provenance-verified dataset for wine expertise, but its utility depends on the release of the corpus and evaluation code.
2608.20106.decisionReason: The paper mentions releasing corpus, audit findings, app, and code, but no direct links or artifact evidence are provided in the input. Without a confirmed public path, the benchmark is deferred.

2608.19957.description: An open benchmark of 3,413 real-world query-code pairs for natural language code retrieval in the 1C:Enterprise ecosystem, with a reproducible evaluation harness and specialized bi-encoder.
2608.19957.whyItMatters: Code retrieval for domain-specific languages is important for developer productivity. This benchmark addresses a gap for 1C:Enterprise, but without accessible data and evaluation tools its comparability cannot be assessed.
2608.19957.decisionReason: The paper describes an open benchmark but does not provide direct links or evidence of released artifacts in the supplied input. Thus, the public reuse path is missing.

2608.20202.description: Evaluates whether retrieved memories distort LLM reasoning or beliefs via Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion tasks.
2608.20202.whyItMatters: Memory-induced cognitive traps can degrade current task performance despite faithful retrieval, highlighting the need to test reasoning shifts rather than only retrieval accuracy.
2608.20202.decisionReason: The paper presents a new benchmark with tasks and results, but no explicit release of the dataset, code, or evaluation harness is stated in the abstract or links, so a credible public path is unclear.

2608.19901.description: MaliciousSkillBench evaluates malicious Agent Skill detection, consolidating 13 sources into 9,740 skills (7,505 malicious, 2,235 benign) across 11 attack categories. It includes protocols for Random and Source-Disjoint splits, measuring Macro-F1 and false positive rates.
2608.19901.whyItMatters: Addresses fragmentation in malicious-skill datasets by providing a comprehensive benchmark that jointly measures attack detection and benign over-flagging. It highlights source-disjoint performance gaps, guiding development of robust detectors for real-world deployment.
2608.19901.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public project page and clear evaluation protocol (splits, metrics). Skills dataset is fixed and reusable; official project link provided.

2608.20312.description: Introduces Inter-X++, a large-scale benchmark with 11,388 interaction sequences and annotations for tasks spanning generation and perception in human-human interaction.
2608.20312.whyItMatters: Addresses gaps in interaction data fidelity and annotation richness, potentially enabling unified evaluation of modeling approaches.
2608.20312.decisionReason: While benchmark tasks and dataset details are described, no artifact release or public access path is specified, making reproducibility unclear.

2608.20220.description: Contains 202 legal benchmark items across six domains and 24 jurisdictions, evaluating whether LLMs recognize and address missing legally material information.
2608.20220.whyItMatters: Tests an underexplored failure mode in legal AI where queries are underspecified, with public decision value for assessing model reliability.
2608.20220.decisionReason: The paper describes benchmark construction and evaluation but does not state a public release of the dataset or evaluation code, leaving the public reuse path unclear.

2608.19981.description: Multilingual medical benchmark with 1,000 expert-reviewed examples per language across nine languages and three task formats.
2608.19981.whyItMatters: Provides a landscape for assessing cross-lingual medical performance, with potential value for comparing models on low-resource languages.
2608.19981.decisionReason: Despite detailed description, no explicit release of the benchmark data or evaluation code is mentioned, so public accessibility remains uncertain.

2608.20153.description: Contains 175 expert-validated instances from recent theoretical computer science papers with Lean formalizations, evaluating LLMs on end-to-end TCS research tasks.
2608.20153.whyItMatters: Targets a challenging domain where current benchmarks are limited, offering a potential standard for formal reasoning research evaluation.
2608.20153.decisionReason: The benchmark is described with expert-validated instances, but no public release of the dataset, Lean formalizations, or evaluation suite is confirmed.

2608.20009.canonicalNameEvidence: we introduce \emph{ExPhy}, a multi-object trajectory forecasting benchmark
2608.20009.description: A multi-object trajectory forecasting benchmark with 24,000 simulated scenes annotated with object-level mass, friction, and restitution. It provides in-distribution and out-of-distribution splits to evaluate trajectory forecasting and physical property estimation jointly.
2608.20009.whyItMatters: Existing trajectory benchmarks focus only on outcome accuracy, not physical property recovery. ExPhy enables measuring whether models capture the physical rules governing motion, and shows that accurate forecasting does not imply accurate property discovery, guiding model development.
2608.20009.decisionReason: The paper explicitly introduces ExPhy as a benchmark with defined splits, evaluation protocols, and public code/data availability on GitHub, satisfying the criteria for a formal release.

2608.19653.description: DeltaML-Bench evaluates ML agents on 48 tasks from research papers, requiring improvement of published baselines within real repositories. It measures per-run success rate and specification gaming across configurations with time allocations (e.g., 4x6h, 2x12h).
2608.19653.whyItMatters: Benchmarks agents under realistic compute constraints and detects specification gaming, which is critical for trustworthy autonomous ML experimentation. Results show scaffolding design (ARG) improves success and reduces gaming, informing agent development practices.
2608.19653.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public code repository providing implementation and grading utilities. Tasks are fixed and reusable with clear protocol; official code link available.

2608.20204.description: Legal contract scrubbing tasks covering errors such as misuse of defined terms, incorrect references, and inconsistent language.
2608.20204.whyItMatters: No formal evaluations of LLMs for contract scrubbing existed, despite its economic value and routine nature.
2608.20204.decisionReason: The paper introduces the benchmark but provides no evidence of released data, code, or scoring submission; a public reuse path cannot be confirmed.

2608.20107.description: Paired synthetic and real video benchmark for evaluating video object removal, focusing on causal consistency including physical effects like shadows and reflections.
2608.20107.whyItMatters: Existing video object removal benchmarks neglect secondary physical effects, limiting assessment of real-world editing quality.
2608.20107.decisionReason: Insufficient evidence of released data, code, or public submission path; only a paper and project page link are provided.

2608.20318.description: A benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on algorithmic design tasks for recursive self-improvement. It includes 10 frozen research repositories across 10 training algorithm families, with agents given 4 hours to rewrite training algorithms and scored by hidden evaluators on a normalized scale.
2608.20318.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks do not isolate the ability to design training algorithms, which is crucial for recursive self-improvement. This benchmark provides a standardized evaluation for such agents, enabling comparison and tracking progress as systems evolve.
2608.20318.decisionReason: The paper releases the task suite, evaluators, and every scored submission, which establishes a clear public reuse path. The evaluation protocol is well-defined with a fixed scoring scale, and the benchmark is designed for ongoing comparison of AI systems.

2608.14379.description: Evaluates vision-language-action models on reaction-critical manipulation across six dynamic tasks, with configurable latency under synchronous and asynchronous inference in a simulated environment.
2608.14379.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of benchmarks for dynamic interaction scenarios in robotic manipulation, providing a standardized way to assess model performance under reaction-critical conditions.
2608.14379.decisionReason: Named benchmark ReflexBench with clear evaluation object, scoring via task success under latency settings, and a project website offering public access.

2608.11683.description: Comprises 220 expert-crafted queries with 11,543 source-attributed rubrics across six finance use cases, evaluating agents on open-ended analyst-style answers via rubric-based grading.
2608.11683.whyItMatters: Captures the full investor workflow beyond narrow data extraction, offering a harder and broader evaluation that assesses agent quality and efficiency in realistic finance research.
2608.11683.decisionReason: Fully open benchmark with public dataset and grading code, providing a comparable scoring contract via rubrics and a clear public reuse path.

2608.12593.description: Evaluates AI agents on discovery of unknown transformation rules across 70 independent games with seven difficulty tiers, requiring experimentation and rule generalization.
2608.12593.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in benchmarks for scientific discovery in controlled environments, testing the capacity to formulate novel generalizations through interaction.
2608.12593.decisionReason: Named DiG-bench with a defined set of games, win conditions as scoring contract, and a public subset of 21 games for reuse; the rest is private for secure evaluation.

2608.08070.description: Evaluates surgical world models on short-horizon instrument motion prediction and dynamics stability from intraoperative image sequences, focusing on geometric accuracy and temporal coherence.
2608.08070.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized protocol for motion-centric evaluation in surgical world models, addressing the lack of public datasets and metrics aligned with instrument motion planning.
2608.08070.decisionReason: Named SurgWMBench with clear evaluation tasks and metrics, and the paper describes it as a benchmark; public path inferred from the paper's contribution.

2608.08264.description: Evaluates operational skill unlearning in deployed agents across 88 attack episodes, measuring attack success rate and impact-weighted exposure after workflow-level defenses.
2608.08264.whyItMatters: Introduces a measurable benchmark for a new safety problem: preventing agents from rebuilding revoked skills, supporting workflow-level evaluation beyond parameter forgetting.
2608.08264.decisionReason: Named OBLIVION as a controlled benchmark with locked episodes and clear metrics; the paper describes the defense harness, providing a public path.

2608.03794.description: Evaluates LLMs across five database lifecycle phases using tasks like schema design, SQL implementation, and debugging, with a focus on holistic database management capabilities.
2608.03794.whyItMatters: Moves beyond Text-to-SQL to cover the full database lifecycle, revealing trade-offs between specialized and general models and supporting full-stack database intelligence.
2608.03794.decisionReason: Named DBLifeBench with a defined task set and evaluation protocol; referred to as a benchmark with public release implied.

2608.07556.description: Evaluates multi-agent systems on 600 productivity tasks measuring task completion and unauthorized action rate across different coordination architectures.
2608.07556.whyItMatters: Makes authorization preservation a measurable property of MAS design, exposing trade-offs between centralized and decentralized coordination for safe delegation.
2608.07556.decisionReason: Named MasDrift as a benchmark with 600 tasks and clear metrics; public path described.

2607.25996.description: Evaluates long-context LLMs on repository-level code reasoning through Output Prediction and Call Chain Prediction tasks, using dynamic tracing and I/O rewriting to reduce memorization.
2607.25996.whyItMatters: Assesses cross-file reasoning capabilities that are critical for real-world software engineering, identifying limitations beyond function-level benchmarks.
2607.25996.decisionReason: Named RepoReasoner with defined tasks and metrics; paper describes benchmark construction and evaluation, implying a public dataset.

2607.13621.description: UESF-Bench evaluates embodied agents on unified language-guided human seeking and following in dynamic environments, covering semantic-guided exploration, behavior switching, and identity grounding across single- and multi-person settings. Scoring uses success metrics for both phases.
