2607.13621.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks assume the target is visible at start, missing realistic scenarios where agents must first find and then follow. UESF-Bench provides a unified evaluation to advance embodied agents in more practical human-robot interaction.
2607.13621.decisionReason: Provides a large-scale benchmark with clear task definition and evaluation protocol, and is posted on arXiv with official links.

2607.01728.description: WUICC-bench evaluates image change captioning for web UI visual regression testing, using natural language descriptions of UI changes. Scoring includes caption quality metrics and assesses suppression of non-meaningful noise.
2607.01728.whyItMatters: Pixel-level VRT is semantically blind and produces false positives. This benchmark enables development of change captioning systems that describe UI changes in words, improving regression testing efficiency.
2607.01728.decisionReason: Introduces a new task with a dataset and benchmark, detailed in the paper with official arXiv links.

2607.02007.description: EduArt evaluates art-historical knowledge and visual reasoning in multimodal LLMs using 871 human-authored questions in Italian and English, covering multiple formats and languages. Scoring is based on accuracy and psychometric properties.
2607.02007.whyItMatters: General benchmarks don't reveal discipline-specific capabilities. EduArt provides a fine-grained benchmark to assess art historical knowledge, showing that format significantly affects performance.
2607.02007.decisionReason: Presents a benchmark dataset with 871 questions and detailed evaluations, supported by official arXiv links.

2606.29894.description: SABER-Math evaluates information retrieval for mathematical queries, with about 283K problems and tasks for reranking based on fine-grained relevance. Scoring uses preference tournament ratings.
2606.29894.whyItMatters: Existing IR benchmarks fail to capture mathematical relevance, and MTEB doesn't predict math performance. SABER-Math provides a math-specific benchmark to guide retriever selection.
2606.29894.decisionReason: Introduces a fully automated benchmark with large-scale data and clear evaluation, official links available on arXiv.

2606.17391.description: NarrativeWorldBench evaluates long-horizon narrative generation in audio drama across nine structural metrics and four Indic languages, across horizons from 10 to 200 episodes. Scoring is based on plot-beat F1 and other metrics.
2606.17391.whyItMatters: Current LLMs degrade on long-horizon narrative coherence. This benchmark provides metrics for evaluating long-form structured content generation and cross-lingual capabilities.
2606.17391.decisionReason: Provides an open benchmark with defined metrics and evaluation across models, official arXiv link provided.

2606.17339.description: SpeechDx evaluates clinical speech AI across 12 datasets and 27 tasks covering various conditions, structured by speech production stages. Scoring includes classification accuracy and zero-shot transfer performance.
2606.17339.whyItMatters: Clinical speech AI lacks comparable evaluation across conditions. SpeechDx provides a shared framework to assess generalization and representation quality, guiding progress toward general-purpose models.
2606.17339.decisionReason: Offers a large-scale benchmark with multiple datasets and tasks, supported by official arXiv links.

2606.17266.description: SkillChain-Gym evaluates production-inventory control policies with reskilling dynamics, including skill certification, forgetting, and training constraints. Metrics cover operations, resilience, capability growth, and training access across seeded disruption scenarios.
2606.17266.whyItMatters: Workforce skills are often overlooked in production benchmarks. SkillChain-Gym provides a testbed to evaluate adaptive policies under skill dynamics, aiding in workforce planning and operational resilience.
2606.17266.decisionReason: Presents a benchmark specification with defined metrics and evaluation protocol, official arXiv link provided.

2606.17328.description: MemTrace evaluates long-term memory in LLM agents at the knowledge point level, probing memory age, question type, and evidence condition. Scoring is based on accuracy across these dimensions.
2606.17328.whyItMatters: Aggregated accuracy misses important memory behaviors. MemTrace provides finer-grained metrics to reveal bottlenecks in evidence use, guiding improvements in memory systems.
2606.17328.decisionReason: Introduces a benchmark with a novel unit of measurement and controlled dimensions, official arXiv link provided.

2606.15684.description: Evaluates multi-agent collaboration in Minecraft-based tasks with time-sensitive complementary collaboration, requiring agent heterogeneity, mandatory collaboration, and dynamic environments. The framework generates diverse tasks via YAML specifications and filters invalid configurations.
2606.15684.whyItMatters: Bridges the gap between static multi-agent benchmarks and real-world scenarios needing real-time coordination under partial observability. Provides a feasibility-aware pipeline for reproducible task generation and evaluation of LLM-based agents in dynamic settings.
2606.15684.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined tasks, scoring via feasibility filter and LLM evaluation, and public framework for task generation and inspection.

2606.12608.description: Assesses multi-turn conversational shopping assistants across 525 expert-authored missions with importance-weighted binary rubrics. Evaluates reasoning across five categories covering preference refinement, trade-off analysis, and compatibility assessment.
2606.12608.whyItMatters: Fills the lack of benchmarks for open-ended shopping dialogue with objective criteria and nuanced reasoning, providing a standardized testbed for improving assistant performance in real-world e-commerce.
2606.12608.decisionReason: Expert-authored benchmark with defined missions and rubric-based scoring, publicly available for model evaluation on Hugging Face.

2606.09450.description: Evaluates LLMs on theorem proving in Lean4 using classical theorems, with two versions: main and premised. Includes metrics for theorem-level coverage and token efficiency to assess partial progress and proof structure.
2606.09450.whyItMatters: Provides a more realistic evaluation of provers beyond contest problems, revealing biases toward easy subtheorems and inefficient proof strategies. Supports finer-grained analysis of formal reasoning capabilities.
2606.09450.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined instances in two forms, releasing data and metrics for reproducible evaluation.

2606.02556.description: Tests rule induction in goal-directed episodic tasks through text games, covering eight tasks across attribute and procedural induction families with controllable lexical grounding and identifiability conditions.
2606.02556.whyItMatters: Evaluates a specific cognitive capability in LLMs, revealing limitations in procedural induction and execution bottlenecks. Provides a structured testbed for studying rule learning and guiding method development.
2606.02556.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined tasks and structural rule forms, enabling reproducibility and comparison across models.

2606.01481.description: Evaluates safety of conditional text-to-video generation using selected start frames and text prompts across 10 malicious categories, measuring unsafety scores and guardrail effectiveness.
2606.01481.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap of safety evaluation when both text and image inputs are benign but output is harmful. Provides a benchmark to improve model safeguards in dynamic video generation.
2606.01481.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined categories and evaluation protocol, publicly available for testing models and guardrails.

2606.01028.description: Provides a continuous-time reinforcement learning environment for dynamic medical treatment recommendation, built from clinical data with physics-informed neural networks. Supports offline and online RL with configurable parameters.
2606.01028.whyItMatters: Offers a realistic testbed for RL methods in continuous-time medical settings, enabling evaluation of personalization, safety, and online deployment gaps. Standardizes comparisons between discrete and continuous time approaches.
2606.01028.decisionReason: Named benchmark environment with clear task definitions and scoring, publicly accessible for research.

2605.29523.description: Evaluates hallucination detection in multi-turn Korean financial RAG dialogues, with a taxonomy based on context answerability. Includes training and test splits for fine-tuning and benchmarking detectors.
2605.29523.whyItMatters: Targets a high-stakes multilingual domain where existing benchmarks lack coverage. Provides a resource to improve hallucination detection and refusal behavior in financial applications.
2605.29523.decisionReason: Named benchmark with constructed dialogues and taxonomy, offering training and evaluation splits for reproducible testing.

2605.29532.description: Evaluates exploratory GUI testing agents on 61 Android apps with 508 preset defects, using an open-set evaluator that decomposes trajectories into independently diagnosable capabilities.
2605.29532.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of open-set evaluation in GUI testing, covering interaction and display defects. Provides a finer-grained assessment of agent capabilities and a verifier integration boost.
2605.29532.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined applications and defects, along with an evaluator for process-aware scoring, available for public use.

2605.28237.description: POINav-Bench evaluates vision-language navigation agents in real-world POI-goal navigation across 11 reconstructed commercial areas covering 126,398 m² with 163 POIs, using traversability-aware annotations and reference trajectories for closed-loop evaluation.
2605.28237.whyItMatters: Existing VLN benchmarks for POI-goal navigation suffer from coarse granularity or sim-to-real gaps. POINav-Bench provides high-fidelity real-world environments, enabling evaluation of final-meters navigation capabilities that are critical for practical deployment.
2605.28237.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (POI-goal navigation in reconstructed real-world areas), scoring via successful arrival, and public path via paper and data availability.

2605.23629.description: DDX-TRACE evaluates medical diagnostic trajectories in multimodal neuroradiology over 211 physician-adjudicated cases, where models request imaging studies, update differential diagnoses, and stop with a localized final diagnosis under hidden evidence.
2605.23629.whyItMatters: Traditional medical AI benchmarks reward final answers, overlooking workup quality. DDX-TRACE measures evidence-supported diagnostic processes, providing a more realistic and actionable evaluation for clinical decision support.
2605.23629.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation protocol (sequential workup with hidden evidence), scoring on trajectory quality, and public availability via paper.

2605.22175.description: SWE-Mutation evaluates LLM-generated test suites in software engineering by using 2,636 mutated variants derived from 800 original instances across nine programming languages, measuring verification and detection rates.
2605.22175.whyItMatters: High-quality test suites are critical for program repair and reinforcement learning signals. SWE-Mutation reveals inadequacies in LLM-generated tests, guiding improvements in code generation and validation.
2605.22175.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined evaluation object (test suite quality via mutation analysis), scoring contract based on detection rates, and public path via paper.

jetbrains-kotlin-benchmark-2026.description: Evaluates AI coding agents on real-world Kotlin tasks from nine open-source repositories. The benchmark uses reproducible Docker environments, regression tests, and a scoring protocol that awards pass only when all expected test transitions are met.
jetbrains-kotlin-benchmark-2026.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the lack of reference evaluation for Kotlin-specific coding agents, providing a reproducible, task-level framework for comparing agent performance on real-world Kotlin issues and tracking progress.
jetbrains-kotlin-benchmark-2026.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a defined task set, reproducible execution via Harbor, and a public scoring contract; official code repository provides a clear reusable path.

github:mounikaperisetti/wexa-ai-benchmar.description: Benchmark framework for managed graph databases using OGB ogbl-collab dataset and workload suite, but published run only measured one database due to missing credentials.
github:mounikaperisetti/wexa-ai-benchmar.whyItMatters: A complete comparison would help evaluate graph database performance for graph workloads, but current results are incomplete for cross-system ranking.
github:mounikaperisetti/wexa-ai-benchmar.decisionReason: Only one database was measured; no comparable scoring across intended databases because other credentials were unavailable, so it lacks a stable completed benchmark.

github:iacker/uncensored-llm-benchmark.description: Planned harness for uncensored open-weight LLMs covering tool calling, code, long context, refusal, factuality, and latency; task suites and first results are not yet implemented.
github:iacker/uncensored-llm-benchmark.whyItMatters: Could fill an evaluation gap for agentic deployments of derestricted models, especially around tool calling and long-context capabilities.
github:iacker/uncensored-llm-benchmark.decisionReason: Harness scaffold exists but task suites and results are pending; the roadmap indicates no completed evaluation or scoring contract yet.

github:aryanthemscoder/recoveriq.description: The repository presents a revenue recovery engine with a benchmark comparing baseline, ML, and agentic policies on 10,000 synthetic payment cases, reporting recovery rate, expected recovery, human review, and unsafe actions.
github:aryanthemscoder/recoveriq.whyItMatters: This benchmark may help evaluate AI-assisted revenue recovery policies in a simulated environment, but no formal benchmark name or stable public comparison protocol is evident.
github:aryanthemscoder/recoveriq.decisionReason: No formally declared benchmark name; the 'benchmark' is an internal experiment within a project README without a defined evaluation contract or public submission path.

github:lvxinquan/rag-benchmark.description: Toolkit under development for evaluating RAG systems across retrieval, context, generation, citations, and system performance, with no published evaluation outputs.
github:lvxinquan/rag-benchmark.whyItMatters: A staged evaluation approach could isolate failure points in RAG pipelines, but without implemented metrics or datasets the value is not yet assessable.
github:lvxinquan/rag-benchmark.decisionReason: Foundation release only defines scope and principles; no metric implementation or benchmark results exist to constitute a usable benchmark.

huggingface:pxzleo/qwen3.8-27b-inference.description: Benchmark evaluating inference throughput and accuracy of four serving configurations for Qwen3.8-27B on RTX 4090. Includes performance metrics per request and accuracy scores on three suites, with protocol and metadata.
huggingface:pxzleo/qwen3.8-27b-inference.whyItMatters: Provides reproducible comparison of local LLM serving options on consumer hardware, covering latency, throughput, and accuracy trade-offs relevant for deployment decisions.
huggingface:pxzleo/qwen3.8-27b-inference.decisionReason: Named benchmark with stable evaluation protocol, scoring formulas, accuracy rerun policy, and released data/metadata. Publicly accessible via Hugging Face and GitHub.

github:gbbarra/llm-summarization-benchma.description: Evaluates reference-faithful summarization of a technical report in Brazilian Portuguese by local LLMs, with a pre-registered rubric scoring fidelity, coverage, format, and fluency across multiple runs.
github:gbbarra/llm-summarization-benchma.whyItMatters: Addresses scarcity of faithfulness benchmarks in Portuguese, providing a reproducible protocol for evaluating local LLMs on strict faithfulness and speed on consumer hardware, which aids model selection for constrained environments.
github:gbbarra/llm-summarization-benchma.decisionReason: Formally named benchmark with DOI, complete protocol, raw outputs, and evaluation criteria publicly available on GitHub and Zenodo, providing a clear public path for reuse.

github:miolonixc/llm-free-benchmark.description: Evaluates free-tier LLMs on OpenRouter and Nous Portal using a fixed battery of seven tasks covering logic, brevity, Russian formatting, reasoning, code generation, regex, and OOP. Each answer is graded programmatically on a 0-5 scale, generating a ranked report.
github:miolonixc/llm-free-benchmark.whyItMatters: Provides a lightweight, dependency-free tool for comparing free-tier model quality in a structured way, addressing the lack of standardized evaluations for no-cost LLM endpoints, which is relevant for developers selecting free options for constrained budgets.
github:miolonixc/llm-free-benchmark.decisionReason: The repository is a newly created GitHub project without independent publication or adoption evidence; the README describes a benchmark but does not formally declare a canonical benchmark name.

github:heretek-ai/harness-benchmark.description: Automated framework for evaluating AI coding harnesses, MCP servers, LSP diagnostics, and agent plugins across coder_eval and terminal-bench.
github:heretek-ai/harness-benchmark.whyItMatters: It standardizes comparisons of coding agents by ablating layers such as LSP, skills, and MCP, but reuses existing benchmarks rather than providing a new evaluation object.
github:heretek-ai/harness-benchmark.decisionReason: The repository is a harness for running existing benchmarks (coder_eval, terminal-bench) rather than a named benchmark with its own task suite and scoring contract.

github:gauthamrohan/financial-sentiment-.description: Benchmark comparing four approaches to financial-news sentiment classification on a fixed 300-sentence subset, measuring macro-F1, latency, and cost across fine-tuned and prompted models.
github:gauthamrohan/financial-sentiment-.whyItMatters: Provides reproducible comparison of fine-tuning versus prompting for a structured classification task, with implications for cost and speed in practical applications.
github:gauthamrohan/financial-sentiment-.decisionReason: Named benchmark with frozen test subset, seeded splits, and clear scoring metric. Code and data available in repository with instructions for replication.

github:kyanitelabs/delegation-bench.description: Design for a delegated task benchmark that certifies safe handoff to local models with confidence floors, judge protocols, and a sabotage safety cell.
github:kyanitelabs/delegation-bench.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of benchmarks that turn capability scores into a personal delegation decision with reliability floors.
github:kyanitelabs/delegation-bench.decisionReason: The scoring contract is defined (exact confidence floors and decision table), but the holdout set is sealed and no run has been executed; the runner and results are not yet published.

github:abdullahuseyinli-dot/annomi-couns.description: A reproducible NLP benchmark for therapist-behaviour classification on the AnnoMI counselling-dialogue corpus, evaluating transcript-grouped classification of therapist utterances into categories such as reflection, question, therapist input, or other.
github:abdullahuseyinli-dot/annomi-couns.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the need for reproducible evaluation in mental-health dialogue analysis, providing a clear protocol for comparing models on sensitive counselling data with proper leakage prevention and uncertainty quantification.
github:abdullahuseyinli-dot/annomi-couns.decisionReason: The repository is a newly created GitHub project with no formal release, independent paper, or official benchmark site; the README does not declare a formal benchmark name, and the name 'AnnoMI Counselling Dialogue Analysis' is descriptive rather than an official benchmark title. Per policy, defer.

github:aiondadotcom/ai-sim-benchmark.canonicalName: AI Coding Agent Water Simulation Benchmark
github:aiondadotcom/ai-sim-benchmark.canonicalNameEvidence: # AI Coding Agent Water Simulation Benchmark
github:aiondadotcom/ai-sim-benchmark.description: A coding challenge for comparing autonomous AI agents on a 3D water simulation task, measuring maximum capability without time or budget constraints.
github:aiondadotcom/ai-sim-benchmark.whyItMatters: Addresses the need for reproducible evaluation of autonomous coding agents on a complex, self-contained task, focusing on capability rather than speed or cost.
github:aiondadotcom/ai-sim-benchmark.decisionReason: Repository is a discovery, not a formal release; no independent paper or official site, and no stable scoring contract defined.

github:ajbermudezh22/agent-model-bench.description: A small benchmark evaluating tool calling and strict JSON output, scored for correctness and formatting discipline, with latency and cost metrics.
github:ajbermudezh22/agent-model-bench.whyItMatters: Fills an evaluation gap by focusing on capabilities agent frameworks rely on, distinguishing models on formatting adherence, which is critical for production glue code.
github:ajbermudezh22/agent-model-bench.decisionReason: GitHub repository with clear README declaring benchmark name, evaluation protocol, scoring contract, and public code for reuse.

github:drivelineresearch/vast-benchmarki.canonicalNameEvidence: Vast Benchmarking Measure the hardware capacity a rented container can actually use.
github:drivelineresearch/vast-benchmarki.description: Bounded benchmark for comparing Vast.ai Docker offers on GPU throughput, effective CPU concurrency, single-thread CPU speed, memory bandwidth, and storage performance, with a 540-second wall-clock budget.
github:drivelineresearch/vast-benchmarki.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized, reproducible way to evaluate rented cloud GPU containers on actual achievable performance, supporting cost-effective hardware selection for compute workloads.
github:drivelineresearch/vast-benchmarki.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository with formal benchmark name, detailed methodology, scoring contracts, and SQLite leaderboard; explicit public release and MIT license.

huggingface:opentwbench/tw-bench.description: Multiple-choice question benchmark from Taiwanese professional exams, covering 16 fields with over 100K questions in Traditional Chinese, structured similarly to tw-exam-bench but with a different dataset identifier.
huggingface:opentwbench/tw-bench.whyItMatters: Provides an alternative or complementary evaluation resource for Traditional Chinese language models, with domain coverage across professional fields.
huggingface:opentwbench/tw-bench.decisionReason: Public Hugging Face dataset with formal metadata and data files; appears to be a variant or duplicate of tw-exam-bench, but stands as a reusable evaluation dataset.

github:kadirnar/turkish-llm-benchmark.description: Provider-neutral benchmark suite for Turkish LLMs measuring quality, instruction following, latency, API cost, and local throughput using 12 Turkish tasks, supporting OpenAI-compatible endpoints and OpenRouter.
github:kadirnar/turkish-llm-benchmark.whyItMatters: Fills the gap for standardized Turkish language model evaluation, offering reproducible comparisons across hosted and local models with cost and performance metrics for practical deployment decisions.
github:kadirnar/turkish-llm-benchmark.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository with formal name, tasks, scoring methodology, and reproducibility features; designed for ongoing model comparison with flexible provider support.

huggingface:thomasip/terminal-bench-3.0-.description: Contains sanitized agent trajectories and scores from a single evaluation of the Ox Alpha model on Terminal-Bench 3.0 tasks.
huggingface:thomasip/terminal-bench-3.0-.whyItMatters: Offers raw data for analyzing a specific model's agentic performance, but lacks a standalone, repeatable evaluation protocol for general model comparison.
huggingface:thomasip/terminal-bench-3.0-.decisionReason: Uses an existing benchmark (Terminal-Bench 3.0) and presents results for a single model without providing a new scoring contract or public reuse path for other submissions.

github:rishidar-lab/sourcelens.description: SourceLens is a RAG application for evidence-grounded document Q&A with citation integrity and prompt-injection defenses.
github:rishidar-lab/sourcelens.whyItMatters: Demonstrates engineering techniques for trustworthy RAG, but does not provide a benchmark protocol for comparing multiple models or systems.
github:rishidar-lab/sourcelens.decisionReason: Primarily a system implementation with internal evaluation artifacts, lacking a defined scoring contract or public path for other teams to submit and compare models.

github:rhs2/sentiment-ml-benchmark.description: Evaluates classical and neural sentiment classifiers on three text datasets using leakage-free protocols and extensive MLOps integration.
github:rhs2/sentiment-ml-benchmark.whyItMatters: Provides a rigorous comparison of sentiment models, but appears tailored to support one paper's findings rather than offering a general submission system.
github:rhs2/sentiment-ml-benchmark.decisionReason: No evidence of ongoing score submission or public leaderboard; the repository serves as a replication and engineering showcase rather than a reusable benchmark others can submit to.

github:wwewtech/russian-it-community-cor.canonicalNameEvidence: **RICC** (**R**ussian **I**T **C**ommunity **C**orpus) is an open data engineering and curation stack
github:wwewtech/russian-it-community-cor.description: A large-scale Russian IT community conversational dataset with tools for data engineering, anonymization, and preparation of SFT, DPO, and RAG training data; includes a suite for local LoRA fine-tuning on consumer hardware.
github:wwewtech/russian-it-community-cor.whyItMatters: Provides a substantial resource for training and evaluating Russian-language technical LLMs, addressing the scarcity of domain-specific conversational data and demonstrating scalable data curation pipelines.
github:wwewtech/russian-it-community-cor.decisionReason: Described as a corpus and data-engineering platform, not as a benchmark with a defined evaluation task or scoring contract.

github:4esv/roman-numeral-harmony-benchm.canonicalNameEvidence: pretty_name: "Roman Numeral Harmony Benchmark: Functional Harmony from Notation"
github:4esv/roman-numeral-harmony-benchm.description: Evaluates music-theory reasoning with four synthetic tasks: chord-symbol, note, pitch-class to Roman-numeral analysis with cadence classification and key identification; scoring is exact match against deterministic gold labels.
github:4esv/roman-numeral-harmony-benchm.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in evaluating LLM reasoning in formal symbolic domains, providing a reproducible benchmark with clear human-interpretable scoring that could inform applications in music education and analysis.
github:4esv/roman-numeral-harmony-benchm.decisionReason: Explicitly called a benchmark with deterministic evaluation and exact-match scoring; results and code released.

github:audn-ai/refusal-benchmark.canonicalNameEvidence: # refusal-benchmark > 519+ harmful prompts to detect how abliterated AI models are.
github:audn-ai/refusal-benchmark.description: A tool that sends a fixed set of harmful prompts to OpenAI-compatible endpoints and classifies responses as refusal, comply, empty, or error to measure refusal rates of served models.
github:audn-ai/refusal-benchmark.whyItMatters: Addresses the practical need to assess safety alignment of deployed models, but lacks a formal task definition, scoring contract, and standardized comparison procedure.
github:audn-ai/refusal-benchmark.decisionReason: Presented as a measurement tool rather than a benchmark with formal evaluation protocol; no clear scoring contract or comparison methodology.

huggingface:ahmedbargady/qwen3.8-27b-ben.description: Presents benchmark evaluation metrics from lm-evaluation-harness for Qwen3.8-27B models on GSM8K and HellaSwag, including throughput telemetry.
huggingface:ahmedbargady/qwen3.8-27b-ben.whyItMatters: Records performance data for specific model versions under standardized hardware, but uses existing benchmarks and does not introduce a new evaluation object or scoring contract.
huggingface:ahmedbargady/qwen3.8-27b-ben.decisionReason: The dataset reports results from established benchmarks rather than defining a new benchmark, so it does not qualify as an original benchmark for this index.

github:msavdert/mandate-bench.canonicalNameEvidence: # Mandate Bench Behavioral benchmarking of LLM agents on a fixed portfolio-rebalancing task
github:msavdert/mandate-bench.description: Behavioral benchmark for LLM agents on a fixed portfolio-rebalancing task, measuring mandate compliance, decision consistency, and reasoning-action agreement; includes a leaderboard with published results.
github:msavdert/mandate-bench.whyItMatters: Provides a noise-resistant alternative to profit-based trading benchmarks, focusing on instruction-following and reliability of LLM agents in financial decision-making, which is crucial for real-world deployment.
github:msavdert/mandate-bench.decisionReason: Explicitly named benchmark with pre-registered experiments, clear metrics, and a public leaderboard; code and results available.

github:ishant-005/llm-finetuning-benchma.canonicalNameEvidence: # llm-finetuning-benchmark Benchmarked different fine tuning strategies like full ft, LoRA, QLoRA.
github:ishant-005/llm-finetuning-benchma.description: A project that benchmarks fine-tuning strategies on a specific dataset and base model, evaluating performance metrics versus cost and memory, and builds a modular multi-adapter system.
github:ishant-005/llm-finetuning-benchma.whyItMatters: Could offer practical insights into fine-tuning trade-offs, but lacks a formal evaluation object, scoring contract, and public reuse path; presented as a one-off comparison.
github:ishant-005/llm-finetuning-benchma.decisionReason: Described as a benchmarking exercise, not a formally named benchmark release with a repeatable evaluation object and scoring contract.

github:vsmirlis/llm-coding-benchmark.description: Compares 31 LLMs on a single browser-based falling-block game coding task, with subjective scoring across gameplay, presentation, prompt adherence, and code quality.
github:vsmirlis/llm-coding-benchmark.whyItMatters: Offers hands-on qualitative comparisons of coding ability, but the scoring is subjective and not designed as a stable, repeatable benchmark for external submissions.
github:vsmirlis/llm-coding-benchmark.decisionReason: The project is explicitly described as a personal evaluation with judgment-based scoring, lacking a standardized, objective scoring contract and credible public reuse path.

github:waynehaha/llm-case-benchmark.description: A platform for running and comparing LLM outputs on user-defined cases, with manual scoring and publishing of snapshots.
github:waynehaha/llm-case-benchmark.whyItMatters: Facilitates ad-hoc model comparisons, but does not define a fixed evaluation object or comparable scoring contract; it is a tool, not a benchmark.
github:waynehaha/llm-case-benchmark.decisionReason: The primary deliverable is a web application for running prompts and viewing outputs, without a standardized task suite or scoring metric that would allow consistent benchmarking.

github:zara-stack/imbalanced-classificat.description: Compares classification strategies on synthetic imbalanced datasets across multiple imbalance ratios using Kappa, G-Mean, and AUC.
github:zara-stack/imbalanced-classificat.whyItMatters: Demonstrates the effect of imbalance on model performance, but it is a single experiment with generated data, not a reusable benchmark with fixed test sets.
github:zara-stack/imbalanced-classificat.decisionReason: The project investigates method behavior on synthetic data without establishing a fixed evaluation object or public scoring protocol for external comparison.

github:junglehek/harness-nlp-benchmark.description: Plans to evaluate DeepSeek Harness and OpenAI Codex on five NLP data engineering tasks to separate model and harness effects.
github:junglehek/harness-nlp-benchmark.whyItMatters: Aims to fill a gap in understanding harness influence in domain-specific NLP workflows, but the benchmark is still in progress with no stable results or final protocol.
github:junglehek/harness-nlp-benchmark.decisionReason: The repository shows an experimental design and task definitions, but no completed results and an unfinished scoring pipeline, so it cannot yet be assessed as a public benchmark.

huggingface:eigenformai/groundtruth-dyna.description: Geology-specific question sets and grading rubrics for evaluating LLMs on real-world geological reasoning, with configs for different geological domains and a leaderboard for submitted runs.
huggingface:eigenformai/groundtruth-dyna.whyItMatters: Provides a domain-specific benchmark for geological reasoning, with evidence-grounded rubrics, enabling evaluation of LLMs in specialized professional fields.
huggingface:eigenformai/groundtruth-dyna.decisionReason: Clear benchmark definition with public dataset, scoring rubrics, and leaderboard; harness and submissions dataset available.

github:shubhraj5575/frontier-agent-bench.description: A benchmarking platform for evaluating autonomous AI engineering agents on engineering quality dimensions such as completion, reliability, testing, architecture, and documentation.
github:shubhraj5575/frontier-agent-bench.whyItMatters: Provides a holistic alternative to code-volume metrics for assessing agent performance, useful for comparing agent development approaches.
github:shubhraj5575/frontier-agent-bench.decisionReason: Presented as a platform for benchmarking, but the evaluation object and scoring contract are configurable by users, not fixed; no standard benchmark definition.

github:chirindaopensource/from_financial.canonicalName: From Financial Sentiment Classification to Return Predictability: A QLoRA Benchmark of Large Language Models
github:chirindaopensource/from_financial.canonicalNameEvidence: From Financial Sentiment Classification to Return Predictability: A QLoRA Benchmark of Large Language Models
github:chirindaopensource/from_financial.description: A research pipeline for evaluating LLMs on financial sentiment classification and return predictability using QLoRA adaptation, with evaluation on multiple financial text datasets and economic metrics.
github:chirindaopensource/from_financial.whyItMatters: Addresses how well LLMs can connect financial NLP to economic prediction, providing evidence on whether sentiment classification transfers to return predictability. The staged approach examines benchmark stability across dataset scales.
github:chirindaopensource/from_financial.decisionReason: Repository is a new implementation of an unreferenced arXiv paper; it references Luo's (2026) benchmark but provides no independent formal release or peer-review evidence, and no stable scoring contract is defined in the provided artifacts.

github:bagheri365/evallab.canonicalNameEvidence: EvalLab is a research-style evaluation project for local LLMs.
github:bagheri365/evallab.description: A research-style evaluation suite for local LLMs measuring model ranking trustworthiness via paired comparisons, benchmark stability, and uncertainty quantification on a fixed set of Python coding tasks.
github:bagheri365/evallab.whyItMatters: Highlights how benchmark composition and sampling can reverse model ranking conclusions, providing tools to assess confidence in LLM comparisons rather than a single leaderboard.
github:bagheri365/evallab.decisionReason: Repository provides a frozen benchmark and scoring protocol, but it is primarily a research project investigating evaluation methodology, not a formally named benchmark release for ongoing public comparison.

github:xiejhhhhhh/euclid-x-desi-q1-multi.description: A galaxy cutout dataset and a bounded benchmark testing how transparent image-statistics models reconstruct a deterministic four-state catalogue rule derived from Euclid and DESI data.
github:xiejhhhhhh/euclid-x-desi-q1-multi.whyItMatters: Addresses the need for auditable construction and reproducible evaluation in astronomy, providing a calibration framework for image-to-catalogue-rule modeling.
github:xiejhhhhhh/euclid-x-desi-q1-multi.decisionReason: The benchmark is not openly accessible: raw data and the embedding table remain restricted, and the public path for third-party evaluation is unclear.

github:snyderconsulting/delverl.canonicalNameEvidence: DelveRL is a human-playable, turn-based roguelike built as an open benchmark for local game-playing agents.
github:snyderconsulting/delverl.description: A human-playable, turn-based roguelike environment for benchmarking local game-playing agents, with deterministic procedural generation, observation/action APIs, a recurrent PPO trainer, and benchmark audits.
github:snyderconsulting/delverl.whyItMatters: Provides a structured environment to study agent capabilities in long-horizon, partially observable decision-making, addressing the need for reproducible game benchmarks beyond single-step tasks.
github:snyderconsulting/delverl.decisionReason: Repository includes benchmark protocol and released baselines, but the benchmark name is not formally declared in a paper or official site; it is presented as a project and benchmark but lacks independent formal release evidence.

github:caitlin-leonard/ct-segmentation-b.canonicalNameEvidence: Multi-Organ CT Segmentation Benchmark — MOOSE vs TotalSegmentator vs VoxTell
github:caitlin-leonard/ct-segmentation-b.description: A staged benchmark comparing three automated organ-segmentation tools (MOOSE, TotalSegmentator, VoxTell) on public CT datasets using Dice and IoU metrics across up to 16 organs.
github:caitlin-leonard/ct-segmentation-b.whyItMatters: Demonstrates that small pilot studies can yield misleading tool rankings, highlighting the importance of sample size and organ coverage in medical segmentation evaluation.
github:caitlin-leonard/ct-segmentation-b.decisionReason: Repository provides a complete pipeline and technical report, but it is a comparison study rather than a formally declared benchmark with a stable scoring contract for public submissions.

github:tiago369/cross-engine-humanoid-be.description: A benchmark comparing MuJoCo and PyBullet simulation engines on a scripted humanoid squat-and-recover task using the Unitree G1 model, evaluating tracking RMSE, contact forces, and runtime performance.
github:tiago369/cross-engine-humanoid-be.whyItMatters: Provides evidence on how simulation engine choices affect robot learning and evaluation, addressing simulation-to-real transfer and the need for cross-engine standardization.
github:tiago369/cross-engine-humanoid-be.decisionReason: Repository defines a clear task and metrics, but it is a single-author engineering comparison rather than a formally named benchmark with independent publication or community adoption.

github:bhargav0549/wexa-graphdb-benchmar.description: A graph database benchmarking suite comparing CognoDB Cloud against Neo4j, Memgraph, ArangoDB, and FalkorDB on the SNAP wiki-Vote dataset with identical resource caps and query workloads.
github:bhargav0549/wexa-graphdb-benchmar.whyItMatters: Provides performance measurements for graph databases under controlled conditions, but as a take-home assignment its scoring and reuse intent are not established.
github:bhargav0549/wexa-graphdb-benchmar.decisionReason: The repository describes a one-off assignment comparison rather than a stable benchmark with an ongoing scoring contract; no evidence of a maintained leaderboard or standardized scoring protocol for external submissions.

huggingface:tollbench/toll-bench-data.description: A public dataset of resolved deals from Toll Bench, a live benchmark where AI systems attempt to fulfill human wants verified by the person's approval.
huggingface:tollbench/toll-bench-data.whyItMatters: Offers a real-world evaluation of agentic goal completion with human verification, but the dataset alone does not define a repeatable scoring protocol.
huggingface:tollbench/toll-bench-data.decisionReason: Only the dataset is specified; the full benchmark's evaluation and scoring details are not present in the input, making the overall contract unclear.

github:rudycelekli/the-value-engine-benc.description: VEB is an evidence-graded RL environment and benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on multi-touch enterprise-sales negotiation. Agents act as B2B sellers in multi-turn negotiations against a stochastic LLM buyer, graded with a sales-methodology rubric producing scalar rewards and structured diagnostic grades.
github:rudycelekli/the-value-engine-benc.whyItMatters: VEB addresses the need for evaluating long-horizon planning, value framing, price discipline, and honesty under pressure in sales negotiations, which single-turn benchmarks do not stress. It provides a methodology-controlled environment for training and evaluating agents, with a focus on reproducible evaluation and a leaderboard for model comparison.
github:rudycelekli/the-value-engine-benc.decisionReason: Repository provides a runnable RL environment, scenario set, evaluation grid, and explicit verification instructions. License openly permits running and forking the environment, and the repo includes code, data artifacts, and validation protocols.

github:ak8x6/talent-bridge-lebanon.description: An AI career-matching agent for Lebanese CS graduates with a built-in Precision@5 evaluation on 15 labelled CVs against a synthetic job corpus.
github:ak8x6/talent-bridge-lebanon.whyItMatters: Demonstrates a measurable approach to validating semantic job retrieval, but the evaluation is embedded within a specific application rather than a standalone benchmark for model comparison.
github:ak8x6/talent-bridge-lebanon.decisionReason: The repository describes an application feature (evaluation harness) rather than a benchmark designed as a reusable evaluation object with a public comparison path for other teams.

github:saklaniabhimanyu/spark-job-optimi.description: A workload-aware ML framework for predicting PySpark execution time and recommending configurations, validated through real benchmark execution but not presented as a benchmark itself.
github:saklaniabhimanyu/spark-job-optimi.whyItMatters: Addresses practical Spark tuning by learning performance models, though the evaluation is a component of a model development project rather than a fixed benchmark for model comparison.
github:saklaniabhimanyu/spark-job-optimi.decisionReason: The project's focus is on building and validating a recommendation system, with benchmark execution serving as internal validation rather than a public reusable benchmark with a stable scoring contract.

github:json604/silentbug-bench.description: silentbug-bench evaluates LLM agents on detecting silent defects in ML training code. Agents receive a small training repository with an injected defect and must identify the defect from a fixed taxonomy, localize it, and provide a patch. Scoring is automated via a program that applies the patch, retrains, and evaluates six components.
github:json604/silentbug-bench.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the challenge of detecting training defects that do not crash or obviously degrade performance, which are difficult to identify manually. It provides a standardized evaluation for agent performance on code understanding, defect localization, and patch correctness, with clear scoring and baselines.
github:json604/silentbug-bench.decisionReason: Repository includes full task suite, scoring harness, baselines, and results. It defines a clear evaluation protocol with fixed tasks, submission schema, and automated scoring. Public path is the repository itself.

github:hemachandra666/silent-misresoluti.description: This repository provides a benchmark and scorer for detecting silent misresolution in dictation cleanup, where a system deletes a spoken revision but produces grammatically correct output that changes the meaning. It includes a corpus of revision sites and a scoring methodology distinguishing silent from visible errors.
github:hemachandra666/silent-misresoluti.whyItMatters: This benchmark exposes a failure mode in dictation systems that existing metrics like edit rate and WER cannot detect. It quantifies the prevalence of silent misresolution and highlights limitations of current evaluation approaches, which could inform better quality metrics for speech-to-text products.
github:hemachandra666/silent-misresoluti.decisionReason: Evidence indicates the study is primarily to highlight a problem with dictation tools and existing metrics, with a small corpus, limited system coverage, and acknowledged limitations in ground truth. It lacks a clear standalone public comparison path for ongoing model evaluation, and the scoring contract is not fully stabilized.

github:cosbi-research/sbmllm-bench.description: SBMLLM-Bench is a manually curated dataset and benchmark for evaluating LLMs on reconstructing executable systems-biology models from scientific papers. Models convert publications into Antimony models, and performance is measured by simulation success, species recovery, reaction accuracy, and dynamic reproducibility.
github:cosbi-research/sbmllm-bench.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the need for automated model reconstruction in systems biology, which is time-consuming and requires expertise. It provides a standardized evaluation for LLM-based model generation and repair, with clear metrics for structural and dynamic fidelity, facilitating comparison of approaches.
github:cosbi-research/sbmllm-bench.decisionReason: Repository provides dataset, workflow, and metrics. It includes a quick-start, configuration, and performance metrics. The benchmark is designed for reuse by other teams, with clear instructions and a public GitHub repository.

github:aiast1/rtcbench.description: RTCbench evaluates LLMs on commissioning closed-loop control systems. A submission is a controller that is wired to a dynamic process simulation and judged on plant performance. It includes ten plants, safety gates, and an anchored scoring baseline.
github:aiast1/rtcbench.whyItMatters: RTCbench addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs for control engineering tasks beyond theoretical quizzes, focusing on real closed-loop performance. It provides a reproducible benchmark with validated tasks, safety constraints, and variance-aware ranking, useful for comparing models on control commissioning.
github:aiast1/rtcbench.decisionReason: Repository includes task files, scoring harness, baselines, and results. It defines a clear interface for submissions and a scoring contract with safety gates and validation. Public path is the repo itself.

github:crispyberry/openbenchmark.description: OpenBenchmark is a platform for turning agent trajectories into custom benchmarks and ranking models on score, cost, and speed. It allows importing traces, drafting tasks with an AI agent, and running evaluations across models.
github:crispyberry/openbenchmark.whyItMatters: This platform enables organizations to create benchmarks from their own data, potentially improving model selection for specific tasks. However, it is a tool for building benchmarks rather than a defined benchmark itself.
github:crispyberry/openbenchmark.decisionReason: This is a tool for creating custom benchmarks, not a predefined benchmark with a fixed task set and scoring contract. It is a platform that users configure for their own evaluations, so it does not meet the definition of a benchmark for public comparison.

huggingface:bryel-labs/musp-bench.description: MuSP-Bench is a 490-question benchmark for musical score understanding, performance listening, and combined score-performance reasoning. Questions cover short, mid, and long musical spans, with modalities for score (S), performance (P), both (SP), and either source (S/P).
huggingface:bryel-labs/musp-bench.whyItMatters: This benchmark fills a gap in evaluating multimodal understanding of music, combining symbolic score and audio performance. It provides a standardized set with multiple input representations (ABC, MIDI, images, audio) and ablation results, useful for comparing models on music reasoning tasks.
huggingface:bryel-labs/musp-bench.decisionReason: The dataset is openly released on Hugging Face with a clear license and includes all inputs and answers. It has a fixed evaluation protocol with accepted answers and response contracts. Reproducibility is possible via the dataset.

github:taimourmushtaq/medical-nlp-superv.description: Uses the public MTSamples corpus with a custom 5-class organ-system label set to evaluate classical TF-IDF models for clinical specialty classification.
github:taimourmushtaq/medical-nlp-superv.whyItMatters: Reuses an existing public dataset without establishing a new reusable evaluation object; results document a single pipeline rather than a repeatable comparison protocol.
github:taimourmushtaq/medical-nlp-superv.decisionReason: The repository reuses the public MTSamples dataset and provides only a one-off experimental pipeline; it does not release new benchmark data or a distinct persistent evaluation contract.

github:vjeyam/llm-quant-tradeoffs.description: Evaluates Qwen2.5-7B at four quantization levels on existing MedQA and PubMedQA datasets, measuring accuracy, throughput, latency, and format compliance.
github:vjeyam/llm-quant-tradeoffs.whyItMatters: Documents quantization tradeoffs on existing benchmarks but does not create a new evaluation object; it is a set of measurements rather than a reusable benchmark.
github:vjeyam/llm-quant-tradeoffs.decisionReason: The repository uses existing datasets (MedQA, PubMedQA) and existing evaluation metrics without introducing a new benchmark dataset or novel scoring protocol.

github:gorkafs13/euskal-agent-bench.description: euskal-agent-bench evaluates LLM agents in Basque, Spanish, and English on a 30-task battery of extraction, reasoning, tool use, and format compliance. Tasks are presented in each language with localized output contracts and tools, and performance is measured on accuracy, contract compliance, and tool-call validity.
github:gorkafs13/euskal-agent-bench.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in evaluating agentic capabilities in low-resource languages, specifically Basque. It measures not only task accuracy but also the robustness of agentic infrastructure (output contracts, tool use) under language shift, which is critical for deploying LLM systems in multilingual contexts.
github:gorkafs13/euskal-agent-bench.decisionReason: The repository provides a reproducible methodology, task battery, scoring code, and a live leaderboard. It includes verified expected values and native speaker validation. The benchmark is designed for comparing models on these tasks.

github:luongnv89/dgx-spark-llm-lab.description: A benchmark for comparing LLM setups—model, quantization, serving flags, and thinking mode—on the user's own hardware. It runs hidden unit-test-based evaluation suites covering code generation and agentic tasks, and provides a command to apply the winning configuration.
github:luongnv89/dgx-spark-llm-lab.whyItMatters: Public leaderboards often rank models on hardware and settings that differ from real deployments. This benchmark lets users evaluate setups on their own endpoint, providing actionable configuration choices. It also reveals trade-offs between thinking mode, cost, and task type.
github:luongnv89/dgx-spark-llm-lab.decisionReason: The repository provides a repeatable evaluation object with hidden tests and a clear scoring contract. The code, test suites, and reports are publicly available, and the tool can be installed and run by others, satisfying the public reuse path.

huggingface:nyamtulla/benchmarking-the-b.description: Evaluates automated safety benchmarks for small language models by scoring 26 SLMs on four existing safety benchmark suites using a GPT-4o judge, producing per-prompt ambiguity scores.
huggingface:nyamtulla/benchmarking-the-b.whyItMatters: Reveals that LLM-oriented safety benchmarks are ineffective for SLMs due to high ambiguity rates, contributing to the research gap in reliable safety evaluation for small models.
huggingface:nyamtulla/benchmarking-the-b.decisionReason: The dataset and code are released, but the core scoring is done by a GPT-4o judge, which is proprietary and not fully reproducible. There is no stable numeric scoring contract independent of the judge, and the ranking is shown to be brittle. It serves primarily as data for the paper's viewpoint rather than a standalone benchmark for ongoing comparison. Hence, defer.

github:break-through-tech/automation-any.description: Template repository outline for an AI Studio challenge project, containing placeholder sections for team members, data exploration, model development, and results.
github:break-through-tech/automation-any.whyItMatters: No evaluation object, task, or scoring contract is defined; the repository remains a template with no benchmark content.
github:break-through-tech/automation-any.decisionReason: The repository is a project template with placeholder text and no defined evaluation object, task, scoring protocol, or released artifacts.

huggingface:djalexj/amo-bench-p.description: A 39-problem subset of AMO-Bench for mathematical reasoning, filtered to questions with parser-gradable answer types (number, set, variable). It relies on the official AMO-Bench evaluator for answer extraction and verification, providing a fixed dataset for evaluating reasoning models.
huggingface:djalexj/amo-bench-p.whyItMatters: This subset enables reproducible evaluation of mathematical reasoning without the cost and variability of LLM-based grading. It offers a clear, automated scoring protocol, making it useful for rapid model comparison and regression testing.
huggingface:djalexj/amo-bench-p.decisionReason: The dataset is publicly released on Hugging Face with a defined filtering criterion and references the official evaluator. The scoring contract is parser-based and deterministic, and the data is accessible for any team to run, providing a clear public reuse path.

github:hervemottaran/alzheimer-classific.description: A benchmark comparing 11 machine learning classifiers for Alzheimer's disease detection on a synthetic dataset. It defines a fixed preprocessing, feature selection, cross-validation, and evaluation pipeline in KNIME and Python, with sensitivity as the primary metric.
github:hervemottaran/alzheimer-classific.whyItMatters: This benchmark provides a reproducible comparison of classifiers for a medical screening task, using a public dataset. It offers insights into algorithm trade-offs on a fixed protocol, useful for practitioners selecting models for similar classification problems.
github:hervemottaran/alzheimer-classific.decisionReason: The repository includes a complete KNIME workflow and instructions for downloading the dataset and reproducing the analysis. The evaluation protocol is clearly defined, and the workflow is importable, enabling other teams to run the same comparison.

github:enterpilot/ai-gateway-reproducibl.description: A benchmark that compares AI gateway solutions (GoModel, LiteLLM, Portkey, Bifrost) for LLM serving. It measures latency, throughput, memory, cold start, and image size on a fixed AWS instance, using a one-command reproducible setup.
github:enterpilot/ai-gateway-reproducibl.whyItMatters: This benchmark provides transparent, reproducible performance comparisons for AI gateways, helping teams choose the right infrastructure. It tracks metrics over time, offering practical decision support for deployment.
github:enterpilot/ai-gateway-reproducibl.decisionReason: The repository includes a runnable script (run.sh) that provisions AWS resources, executes the benchmark, and records results. The evaluation protocol is clearly specified with parameters for repeatability, and results are committed publicly, facilitating ongoing comparison.

github:anmol-mahajan/ai-db-benchmark.description: Evaluates database performance and LLM workflow behavior across SQLite, DuckDB, pgvector, Qdrant, Chroma, LanceDB, Milvus, and Weaviate on synthetic enterprise data, measuring retrieval, generation, accuracy, and write-back latency.
github:anmol-mahajan/ai-db-benchmark.whyItMatters: Addresses the need to measure database and LLM integration performance for production-shaped workloads, providing separate metrics for database reads, model reasoning, answer accuracy, and persistence.
github:anmol-mahajan/ai-db-benchmark.decisionReason: The benchmark is specified with detailed CLI commands and deterministic data generation, but the official links include a localhost URL and the project is in early MVP stage; evidence of a complete public release is unclear.

github:jannehyba/therapy-note-bench.description: Reproducible harness for evaluating LLM-generated psychotherapy session notes using two existing datasets (TN-Eval SOAP and iCARE/iHOPE), with automatic scoring tracks planned.
github:jannehyba/therapy-note-bench.whyItMatters: Provides a rerunnable path for comparing LLMs on clinical note generation tasks where prior benchmarks were one-off, potentially enabling more robust model selection in healthcare documentation.
github:jannehyba/therapy-note-bench.decisionReason: The repository is a work in progress with no results yet; scoring and judge calibration are not implemented, so the repeatable scoring contract is not yet established.

github:parfait18/repo-context-ambiguity.canonicalNameEvidence: # repo-context-ambiguity **Do code generation models notice constraints that live in the codebase rather than in the prompt?**
github:parfait18/repo-context-ambiguity.description: Evaluates code generation models on repository-level implicit constraints across 12 tasks with 4 prompt conditions, using automatic AST oracles to detect convention violations and clarification question rates.
github:parfait18/repo-context-ambiguity.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap where code models may satisfy explicit prompts while violating unstated repository conventions, which is undetected by standard test suites and can lead to security and correctness issues in real-world codebases.
github:parfait18/repo-context-ambiguity.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository with methodology, metrics, and harness; automatic oracles provide deterministic scoring; code and data available for reuse.

github:gauthamrohan/rag-retrieval-benchm.description: Compares seven retrieval configurations on 648 FiQA financial queries with gold relevance labels, measuring Recall@10, MRR@10, nDCG@10, and latency, including dense, BM25, hybrid, and reranking pipelines.
github:gauthamrohan/rag-retrieval-benchm.whyItMatters: Provides evidence that common RAG advice (hybrid search plus reranking) can degrade retrieval quality and latency, informing practical retrieval system design for similar domains.
github:gauthamrohan/rag-retrieval-benchm.decisionReason: Repository lacks an explicit declared benchmark name beyond a generic description; despite clear methodology and reproducible code, it is presented as a study rather than a formally named benchmark release.

github:andyast/pi-agent-reliability-benc.description: Compares a cloud coding-agent baseline against local MLX models on six engineering reliability criteria using nine hand-crafted cases with semi-automated scoring.
github:andyast/pi-agent-reliability-benc.whyItMatters: Provides a practical lens on whether local coding models can approach cloud baselines in constraint-following and scope control, which matters for teams with data residency or cost constraints.
github:andyast/pi-agent-reliability-benc.decisionReason: Although the repository is public and provides run scripts, the scoring is semi-automated and requires manual 0-5 ratings, and the small task set is tailored to a specific research comparison; it is not intended as a standalone public leaderboard.

github:cl1110goo-afk/oraclephys.description: Benchmark evaluates LLM fine-tuning objectives on structural mechanics tasks. Models rank stories of steel frames by inter-story drift and identify the governing story. Evaluation axes include forward ranking, extrapolation, two-step horizons, and post-intervention prediction, with exact finite-element oracle truths.
github:cl1110goo-afk/oraclephys.whyItMatters: Provides a controlled testbed to study how different supervision forms affect LLM capabilities in physics-based domains. The exact oracle allows probing whether models learn underlying principles or surface cues, informing training methodology for scientific applications.
github:cl1110goo-afk/oraclephys.decisionReason: Provides static benchmark files, dataset, code, and training pipeline. The source includes evaluation instructions, metrics, and reproducibility notes, and explicitly states public availability.

github:kissmee-star/nlp-benchmark-group1.description: Course project that compares logistic regression and linear SVM on the UCI Sentiment Labelled Sentences dataset using TF-IDF features.
github:kissmee-star/nlp-benchmark-group1.whyItMatters: The comparison of two classical models on a tiny sentiment dataset does not provide a reusable evaluation object or scoring contract for measuring model capability.
github:kissmee-star/nlp-benchmark-group1.decisionReason: This is a one-time student exercise with two models and a small dataset; it lacks a stable benchmark protocol and is not intended for ongoing model comparison.

github:jasmine-phsifai/local-inference-f.description: Measures sustained performance of local OCR and ASR runtimes on a specific Windows CPU-only hardware configuration, with recommendations based on throughput and stability.
github:jasmine-phsifai/local-inference-f.whyItMatters: Provides practical data for choosing local inference runtimes on similar hardware, but the evaluation is tied to a single machine and does not define a standardized scoring contract for cross-system comparison.
github:jasmine-phsifai/local-inference-f.decisionReason: The repository measures runtime performance on one specific hardware setup rather than providing a reusable benchmark with a stable scoring protocol; other teams cannot meaningfully compare models without the same hardware.

github:rzenil/llm-router-benchmark.description: Analyzes LLM router runs from JSONL files, scoring success, quality heuristics, latency, cost, and fallback recovery according to a configurable policy.
github:rzenil/llm-router-benchmark.whyItMatters: Could help teams evaluate router configurations operationally, but the current MVP provides only heuristic quality checks and no fixed task suite or scoring standard for model comparison.
github:rzenil/llm-router-benchmark.decisionReason: The repository is an analysis tool for router logs rather than a defined benchmark with a stable evaluation object; scoring is configurable and quality is heuristic, limiting comparability.

github:jyotydivya/gpu-accelerated-ml-inf.description: Measures inference latency, throughput, and GPU utilization for PyTorch CPU, PyTorch CUDA, and TensorRT on ResNet50 across batch sizes, with an optional Streamlit dashboard for visualization.
github:jyotydivya/gpu-accelerated-ml-inf.whyItMatters: Provides practical comparisons of execution engine performance for GPU-accelerated ML inference, relevant for deployment decisions on latency and resource usage.
github:jyotydivya/gpu-accelerated-ml-inf.decisionReason: Repository appears as a demonstration project rather than a formally defined benchmark with a stable scoring contract and official release; lacks a declared benchmark name and independent evidence of formal validation.

github:suneharaj/financial-hybrid-rag.description: Evaluates retrieval configurations in a financial RAG pipeline using RAGAS metrics on a 50-query golden set.
github:suneharaj/financial-hybrid-rag.whyItMatters: The evaluation harness and reported metrics enable comparison of dense, sparse, hybrid, and reranked retrieval for financial question answering.
github:suneharaj/financial-hybrid-rag.decisionReason: The primary artifact is a software system, and its RAGAS evaluation is a component of that system rather than a standalone benchmark with a public leaderboard or submission path.

github:magna56/ai-commit-2026-08-23-s2-y.description: Probes the sensitivity of a coding-agent benchmark score to container memory limits using a simulated evaluation.
github:magna56/ai-commit-2026-08-23-s2-y.whyItMatters: Demonstrates how infrastructure configuration can confound coding-agent leaderboard scores, showing that memory headroom changes success rates independently of model ability.
github:magna56/ai-commit-2026-08-23-s2-y.decisionReason: The repository supports a single analytical finding and does not provide an independent public benchmark for model comparison.

github:vnish-global/vnish-global-operato.canonicalName: VNISH GLOBAL Multilingual Operator Routing Benchmark
github:vnish-global/vnish-global-operato.canonicalNameEvidence: # VNISH GLOBAL Multilingual Operator Routing Benchmark
github:vnish-global/vnish-global-operato.description: Evaluates AI assistants on routing VNISH operator questions to owned sources, stopping on incomplete evidence, and avoiding device/account actions across 80 cases in ten locales, with a defined scoring contract.
github:vnish-global/vnish-global-operato.whyItMatters: Addresses the need for reliable operator assistance in multilingual contexts where correct source routing and safety constraints are critical, providing a standardized evaluation for agent safety and precision.
github:vnish-global/vnish-global-operato.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository with formal benchmark name, data files, evaluation methodology, and release scope; explicitly declares public release and Apache 2.0 license.

huggingface:opentwbench/tw-exam-bench.description: Multiple-choice question benchmark from Taiwanese professional exams, covering 16 fields with over 100K questions in Traditional Chinese, organized by exam field with test splits available.
huggingface:opentwbench/tw-exam-bench.whyItMatters: Provides a large-scale, domain-specific evaluation for Chinese language models in Traditional Chinese, covering professional knowledge areas crucial for real-world applications in Taiwan.
huggingface:opentwbench/tw-exam-bench.decisionReason: Public Hugging Face dataset with formal name, license, and structured data; clearly a reusable evaluation dataset with stable test split and multiple-choice scoring.

huggingface:ahmedbargady/open-models-ben.description: A leaderboard of evaluation metrics and throughput telemetry for open-weights language models tested on NVIDIA A100 GPUs using established benchmarks GSM8K and HellaSwag.
huggingface:ahmedbargady/open-models-ben.whyItMatters: Aggregates existing benchmark results with standardized hardware and inference settings, but does not introduce a new evaluation task or scoring protocol.
huggingface:ahmedbargady/open-models-ben.decisionReason: The dataset compiles scores from pre-existing benchmarks rather than defining a new benchmark object with its own evaluation contract.

github:guptabhishekumar/grit-benchmark.canonicalNameEvidence: GRIT Grounded Robot Intelligence under Turbulence
github:guptabhishekumar/grit-benchmark.description: Simulated robot planning benchmark where LLM planners must recover from turbulence events; tasks include object teleportation, grip failures, and mid-task instruction changes; scored on recovery.
github:guptabhishekumar/grit-benchmark.whyItMatters: Tests robustness of LLM-based planners in dynamic, adverse environments, filling a gap in evaluating beyond clean-task performance.
github:guptabhishekumar/grit-benchmark.decisionReason: Named benchmark with pre-registered episodes, clear scoring, and public code and logs; includes baseline results.

github:0xboyu/company-mental-model-bench.description: A research benchmark testing whether explicit company economic-model representations improve LLM ability to synthesize investment theses, with three treatments and a frozen evidence set of eight company cases.
github:0xboyu/company-mental-model-bench.whyItMatters: Explores whether structured representations enhance LLM reasoning for investment analysis, providing a framework for comparing synthesis approaches in financial applications.
github:0xboyu/company-mental-model-bench.decisionReason: Repository is a standalone research experiment with a designed benchmark, but no empirical results are claimed yet; it lacks a formal release and public comparison path.

github:anuragkokate09/asr-model-benchmar.description: A reproducible CPU-only benchmark comparing Whisper Small, Faster-Whisper Small, and Wav2Vec2 Base on clean and noisy LibriSpeech subsets, evaluating WER, latency, memory, and robustness.
github:anuragkokate09/asr-model-benchmar.whyItMatters: Provides a controlled comparison of ASR models under specific conditions, helping practitioners choose models based on accuracy and efficiency on CPU hardware.
github:anuragkokate09/asr-model-benchmar.decisionReason: Repository provides a clear evaluation protocol and results but it is a single-author project without formal name declaration or independent release evidence beyond the GitHub page.

github:bluebunnyanon/agent-benchmark-2d-.description: A benchmark for evaluating interactive multimodal agents in structured 2D maze environments, with declarative maze specs, environment implementations, scoring, and a reproducible pipeline.
github:bluebunnyanon/agent-benchmark-2d-.whyItMatters: Addresses evaluation of long-horizon agentic interactions in partially observed environments, providing a structured testbed for agent capabilities beyond single-step prediction.
github:bluebunnyanon/agent-benchmark-2d-.decisionReason: Repository is an anonymous submission with code and benchmark instances, but it lacks a formally declared benchmark name and independent publication evidence, making it a discovery without formal release.

github:t1mdurden/benchmark-resolution.description: Statistical analysis of leaderboard gaps in SWE-bench and tau-bench, computing confidence intervals, McNemar tests, and minimum detectable differences.
github:t1mdurden/benchmark-resolution.whyItMatters: Quantifies the resolving power of existing software engineering benchmarks, revealing that many leaderboard differences fall below detection thresholds.
github:t1mdurden/benchmark-resolution.decisionReason: It is a re-analysis of existing benchmarks rather than a new benchmark with defined evaluation objects and scoring contract.

github:lorien/awesome-ai-benchmarks.description: A curated list of links to AI model and agent benchmarks and rankings.
github:lorien/awesome-ai-benchmarks.whyItMatters: Serves as a handy collection of existing benchmarks for practitioners seeking evaluation resources.
github:lorien/awesome-ai-benchmarks.decisionReason: It is a list of benchmarks, not a benchmark itself.

github:kyashrathore/agent-app-benchmark.canonicalNameEvidence: Agent App Benchmark is a public, reproducible performance benchmark for multi-harness coding-agent GUI applications.
github:kyashrathore/agent-app-benchmark.description: A public benchmark for evaluating GUI performance of coding-agent applications using canonical session data and deterministic scenarios for start, session switching, memory, and CPU, with a repeatable protocol.
github:kyashrathore/agent-app-benchmark.whyItMatters: It provides a standardized, reproducible way to compare GUI responsiveness and resource use across coding-agent tools, supporting tool selection and performance optimization.
github:kyashrathore/agent-app-benchmark.decisionReason: Formally named in README as 'Agent App Benchmark' with public reproducibility, detailed protocol, scoring contract, and canonical corpus with open-source code.

github:viochris/rag-token-benchmark-vect.canonicalName: RAG Token & Cost Benchmark: Vector vs Graph vs Hybrid
github:viochris/rag-token-benchmark-vect.canonicalNameEvidence: # 🔍 RAG Token & Cost Benchmark: Vector vs Graph vs Hybrid
github:viochris/rag-token-benchmark-vect.description: Benchmarks token consumption and inference cost across Vector RAG, Graph RAG, and Hybrid RAG pipelines on identical questions over a YouTube transcript, using LlamaIndex, ChromaDB, Neo4j, and Gemini.
github:viochris/rag-token-benchmark-vect.whyItMatters: Quantifies the token and dollar overhead of adding graph and hybrid retrieval to RAG, helping practitioners with limited API budgets choose cost-effective architectures.
github:viochris/rag-token-benchmark-vect.decisionReason: The repository defines a fixed evaluation protocol with identical questions and transcript, reporting token counts and costs, and code is publicly available for reproduction.

github:prachipmishra/rag-quantization-be.canonicalNameEvidence: # RAGQuantBench A benchmarking tool that measures how LLM quantization — fp16 vs. 8-bit vs. 4-bit — affects RAM usage, latency, and answer quality.
github:prachipmishra/rag-quantization-be.description: Evaluates LLM quantization variants (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit) in a RAG pipeline measuring RAM usage, latency, throughput, and answer quality on the same documents and questions.
github:prachipmishra/rag-quantization-be.whyItMatters: Provides a reproducible framework to compare quantization trade-offs in real RAG workloads, helping practitioners make cost-performance decisions.
github:prachipmishra/rag-quantization-be.decisionReason: The benchmark is formally named RAGQuantBench, has a defined evaluation object, repeatable protocol, scoring metrics, and public code and dashboard for others to run.

github:pxlcrtiv/pocket-eval.description: Evaluates language models on a bundled DeFi/on-chain/ML corpus measuring perplexity and accuracy on a 12-item multiple-choice QA mini-benchmark, with deterministic n-gram and random baselines and optional Hugging Face backend.
github:pxlcrtiv/pocket-eval.whyItMatters: Provides a lightweight, CPU-only, keyless evaluation harness that includes a deterministic chance floor and lexical baseline, enabling reproducible model comparisons without GPU infrastructure.
github:pxlcrtiv/pocket-eval.decisionReason: The repository explicitly defines a self-contained evaluation with a fixed corpus, 12-item QA benchmark, deterministic baselines, and documented scoring commands, allowing other teams to run and compare models.

github:neoxider/neoxider-benchmark.canonicalNameEvidence: # Neoxider Benchmark ![Neoxider Benchmark](docs/cover.png) A small, honest benchmark for **agentic** CLI models
github:neoxider/neoxider-benchmark.description: Eight procedurally generated task suites with ten levels each evaluate instruction following, pathfinding, browser work, spatial reasoning, honesty, arithmetic, solution quality, and tool selection in agentic CLI models.
github:neoxider/neoxider-benchmark.whyItMatters: Measures practical agentic reliability, including resistance to fabrication, with penalties for hallucinated answers and token-cost transparency.
github:neoxider/neoxider-benchmark.decisionReason: The README defines a formal benchmark with tasks, scoring rules, leaderboard, public code, and procedural generation for reproducible evaluation.

github:brncoguz/localslm.canonicalNameEvidence: # LocalSLM LocalSLM is a benchmarking lab for small language models running locally through Ollama.
github:brncoguz/localslm.description: Evaluates locally run small language models via Ollama, recording throughput, time-to-first-answer, memory use, and cold-start cost across chat and benchmark sessions.
github:brncoguz/localslm.whyItMatters: Provides local performance measurements that public leaderboards do not cover, supporting model selection for privacy-sensitive, low-latency, and edge deployments.
github:brncoguz/localslm.decisionReason: GitHub repository with official README declares a repeatable measurement framework and public code/artifact path; comparisons use paired scoring and exclusions.

github:shristijain00/llm-benchmark-tool.description: Evaluates latency, cost, and response quality across multiple LLMs accessed via OpenRouter using a configurable prompt set and deterministic quality heuristics.
github:shristijain00/llm-benchmark-tool.whyItMatters: Provides a mechanical way to compare LLM cost-latency-quality trade-offs on custom prompts, supporting practical model selection decisions.
github:shristijain00/llm-benchmark-tool.decisionReason: The repository provides a tool for running custom comparisons rather than a formally named benchmark release with a fixed evaluation object and comparable scoring contract.

huggingface:mayank-dubey-ai/l4-gpu-llm-b.canonicalName: L4 GPU LLM Serving & Quality Benchmark Leaderboard (vLLM)
huggingface:mayank-dubey-ai/l4-gpu-llm-b.canonicalNameEvidence: pretty_name: "L4 GPU LLM Serving & Quality Benchmark Leaderboard (vLLM)"
huggingface:mayank-dubey-ai/l4-gpu-llm-b.description: Benchmark for open-weight LLMs on a single NVIDIA L4 24GB GPU, evaluating serving performance including TTFT, TPOT, throughput, peak VRAM, energy, and cost alongside quality tasks such as HumanEval+, MMLU-Pro, BFCL v4 tool calling, and RULER needle retrieval.
huggingface:mayank-dubey-ai/l4-gpu-llm-b.whyItMatters: Provides a real-world local deployment benchmark to compare LLM tradeoffs in latency, throughput, energy, and accuracy under vLLM on hardware-constrained L4 GPUs, aiding model selection.
huggingface:mayank-dubey-ai/l4-gpu-llm-b.decisionReason: The benchmark is released on Hugging Face with an explicit compact name, stable scoring contract, and public data/code reuse path; it is intended for model comparison.

huggingface:arcophos/health-optimization.description: A 30-task rubric-graded sample of the full Health Optimization Bench, covering preventive and optimization medicine across ten micro-bench domains with clinician-style requests, binary scoring rubrics, and reference answers.
huggingface:arcophos/health-optimization.whyItMatters: Provides a public, reusable protocol for measuring how language models handle current clinical evidence in preventive medicine, enabling transparent and comparable evaluation on a curated subset.
huggingface:arcophos/health-optimization.decisionReason: The dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face with a clear task format, scoring rubric, and evaluation protocol, and the README explicitly names it as a benchmark sample.

github:tienxion/eeg-privacy-benchmark.canonicalNameEvidence: # EEG Privacy Benchmark v1 A reproducible benchmark for asking a narrow question: when an EEG decoder is trained for left- versus right-hand motor imagery, what subject-identity and training-membership signals remain in its representations and outputs?
