github:tienxion/eeg-privacy-benchmark.description: Evaluates privacy leakage in EEG motor-imagery decoders across BNCI2014-001, Lee2019 MI/OpenBMI, and PhysioNet datasets, measuring subject-identity and training-membership signals under CSP-LDA, EEGNet variants, and attacker models.
github:tienxion/eeg-privacy-benchmark.whyItMatters: Provides a reproducible protocol for comparing privacy defenses on EEG models, separating utility from privacy metrics and exposing where defenses fail across datasets and attackers.
github:tienxion/eeg-privacy-benchmark.decisionReason: Formally named benchmark with versioned release, frozen splits, defined metrics, and public code enabling reproduction and comparison.

huggingface:xnhyacinth/dt-sched-bench-v0.canonicalNameEvidence: # DT-Sched-Bench v0.57.1 Core Protocol-2.1 Core for **DT-Sched-Bench**: LLMs as scheduling and supervisory agents against seeded simulator backends.
huggingface:xnhyacinth/dt-sched-bench-v0.description: Core dataset for evaluating LLMs as scheduling and supervisory agents against seeded simulator backends, with 288 rows and scenario YAMLs.
huggingface:xnhyacinth/dt-sched-bench-v0.whyItMatters: Addresses the need for standardized evaluation of LLM-driven scheduling in simulated environments.
huggingface:xnhyacinth/dt-sched-bench-v0.decisionReason: Hugging Face dataset page lacks independent paper or strong adoption; leaderboard eligibility is false and scoring pending, so not a formal release.

github:ronitloke/docuintel.description: Document processing and RAG platform with a measured retrieval benchmark on DocVQA validation data, comparing keyword, semantic, hybrid, and CrossEncoder reranking.
github:ronitloke/docuintel.whyItMatters: Shows trade-offs between retrieval quality and latency in document Q&A pipelines.
github:ronitloke/docuintel.decisionReason: The repository is a platform with an internal evaluation module, not a standalone benchmark with a public comparison path.

github:kumarkhailendra/cognodb-graph-ben.canonicalNameEvidence: # GraphBench — CognoDB Cloud Benchmark GraphBench is a reproducible benchmark harness for the Wexa AI take-home assignment.
github:kumarkhailendra/cognodb-graph-ben.description: Reproducible benchmark harness for CognoDB Cloud graph database, measuring traversal, lookup, aggregation, and mixed read/write performance using the SNAP Wiki-Vote dataset.
github:kumarkhailendra/cognodb-graph-ben.whyItMatters: Provides a deterministic and transparent method for evaluating graph database performance, including concurrency and latency metrics.
github:kumarkhailendra/cognodb-graph-ben.decisionReason: Formally named benchmark with clear workloads, metrics, and public code enabling independent execution and comparison.

github:sanjuhs/benchmark-math-test.canonicalNameEvidence: # Benchmark Math Test Benchmark Math Test is a hybrid public/private project for learning how AI benchmarks are designed, executed, scored, hosted, and reported.
github:sanjuhs/benchmark-math-test.description: Evaluates short-answer mathematical reasoning across ten categories with 100 public and 400 private questions, supporting model-only and calculator-agent modes.
github:sanjuhs/benchmark-math-test.whyItMatters: Offers a transparent educational benchmark for understanding AI evaluation, including held-out scoring and agentic tool use.
github:sanjuhs/benchmark-math-test.decisionReason: Formally named benchmark with public code, hosted API, and documented scoring protocol enabling independent evaluation.

github:xiaomingx/awesome-security-benchm.description: Curated list of security vulnerability benchmarks and samples for evaluating SAST tools and LLMs.
github:xiaomingx/awesome-security-benchm.whyItMatters: Consolidates resources for security evaluation but does not define a new evaluation protocol.
github:xiaomingx/awesome-security-benchm.decisionReason: It is an aggregation of existing benchmarks and datasets, not a standalone benchmark release.

github:pavanipavani16423-ctrl/ask_db.description: Natural-language analytics copilot over a 7-table SQLite database, with a 25-question internal benchmark for SQL generation accuracy.
github:pavanipavani16423-ctrl/ask_db.whyItMatters: Demonstrates self-repairing SQL generation and read-only guardrails, but the benchmark is for internal validation.
github:pavanipavani16423-ctrl/ask_db.decisionReason: The benchmark is embedded in the application and not released as a standalone evaluation object with a public comparison path.

github:ka2in/ai-detector-benchmark.description: Spot check of three AI text detectors on three samples (human, raw AI, edited AI) to test detection consistency.
github:ka2in/ai-detector-benchmark.whyItMatters: Highlights variability in AI detector responses to human editing, but lacks statistical power and standalone comparison infrastructure.
github:ka2in/ai-detector-benchmark.decisionReason: It is a small illustrative test supporting a single finding, not a repeatable benchmark with a public scoring contract.

github:busybrainx99/ai-agent-web-scrapin.description: Compares ZenRows, Jina, Firecrawl, and CrawlForge across protected and unprotected websites, measuring successful content retrieval, response time, HTTP status, content length, and request cost.
github:busybrainx99/ai-agent-web-scrapin.whyItMatters: Provides a repeatable way to compare web scraping APIs on reliability and speed against common bot protection systems, helping developers choose the right tool.
github:busybrainx99/ai-agent-web-scrapin.decisionReason: The repository defines a fixed set of target URLs, providers, metrics, and a CSV output dataset, along with a public GitHub path for running the benchmark.
